The recruitment was conducted by the H.P. Rajya Chayan Aayog (HPRCA), Hamirpur for the post of Junior Office Assistant (Library) as Job Trainee. The Computer Based Screening Test (CBT) for this recruitment was held on 25.04.2026.

Result Status

The result status is: Final Result Declared. The HPRCA has compiled the final result for 77 posts out of the 78 advertised posts for Junior Office Assistant (Library), Post Code-25024.

Selection Stage Covered

This final result covers the following stages:

  • Computer Based Screening Test (CBT) held on 25.04.2026
  • Document Verification held on 06.06.2026 and 08.06.2026
  • Final Merit-Based Result declared on 06.07.2026

Individual score cards for the Computer Based Screening Test are not mentioned as separately available for download in the official press note. However, the final result itself includes the scores obtained out of 120 by each selected candidate, along with their roll numbers, arranged as per merit.

The merit list of 77 selected candidates is available and has been published along with the final result on the official website of HPRCA, Hamirpur.

Cut Off Marks and Qualifying Marks

Category-wise or post-wise cut off marks have not been officially released separately in the press note. Candidates can refer to the marks listed against each selected roll number in the final result to understand the merit range for their category.

  2. Look for the press note or result notification related to Post Code-25024, Junior Office Assistant (Library).

The HPRCA Junior Office Assistant final result document includes the following details for each selected candidate:

The result also mentions the total number of applications, candidates who appeared, candidates who remained absent, and the number of posts filled against the advertised vacancies.

Candidates whose roll numbers appear in the final selected list should keep their original documents ready and wait for further official communication from HPRCA or the concerned department regarding joining or appointment formalities, as this has not been separately announced in the press note.

Documents Required for the Next Stage

Specific documents required for any further stage after the final result have not been officially announced in this press note, since document verification for this recruitment has already been completed on 06.06.2026 and 08.06.2026.

The selection process for the Junior Office Assistant (Library) Job Trainee post, Post Code-25024, consisted of:

The MPPSC Paediatric Specialist Selection List 2026 has been released by the Madhya Pradesh Public Service Commission (MPPSC) on 6 July 2026 for the post of Paediatric Specialist (Shishu Rog Visheshagya) under the Public Health and Medical Education Department. This is a new revised selection list issued after the Commission cancelled its earlier lists dated 3 September 2025 and 11 June 2026, following directions from the Indore Bench of the Madhya Pradesh High Court. Candidates who applied against Advertisement No. 05/2024 can check the complete details, background of the revision, vacancy breakdown, and official download link below.

Add FJA on  As Preferred Source

MPPSC Paediatric Specialist Selection List 2026: Overview

Particulars Details
Organization Madhya Pradesh Public Service Commission (MPPSC)
Post Name Paediatric Specialist (Shishu Rog Visheshagya)
Department Public Health and Medical Education Department, Government of Madhya Pradesh
Advertisement Number 05/2024 dated 24.07.2024
Selection List Number 4846/52/2024/चयन

Total Advertised Posts 208 (Main part 87% + Provisional part 13%)
Posts Covered in This List 185 (Main part – 87% only)
Selection Stage Final Selection List (based on interview merit)
List Type Revised Selection List (earlier lists cancelled)
Official Website mppsc.mp.gov.in

Release Date and Background

The revised selection list carries reference number 4846/52/2024/चयन and was issued from Indore on 6 July 2026. It relates to Advertisement No. 05/2024 dated 24 July 2024, issued for recruitment to the post of Paediatric Specialist against a total of 208 posts. Interviews of eligible candidates were conducted between 3 July 2025 and from 11 August 2025 to 12 August 2025.

As per a corrigendum dated 27 March 2025, the vacant posts under this advertisement were divided into two parts: a main part covering 87% of posts and a provisional part covering the remaining 13%. Since no eligible candidates were available for the provisional part, the Commission decided that a separate result for the provisional part was not required, and the current list covers only the 185 posts under the main part (87%).

Why the Earlier Selection List Was Cancelled

This is not the first selection list issued for this post. Here is the sequence of events that led to the current revised list:

  • The Commission first declared a selection list (No. 8397/52/2024/चयन) and a marks list (No. 8398/52/2024/चयन) on 3 September 2025.
  • These were later withdrawn, and a revised selection list (No. 3996/52/2024/चयन) along with a revised marks list (No. 3997/52/2024/चयन) were declared on 11 June 2026.
  • Meanwhile, in compliance with orders passed by the Indore Bench of the Madhya Pradesh High Court in Writ Petition No. 12337/2025, Writ Petition No. 39146/2025, and other connected petitions, the Commission conducted additional interviews on 21 May 2026 for candidates named in its notice dated 13 May 2026 (No. 2549/52/2024/चयन).
  • Due to an error during processing of the revised result, 4 candidates whose candidature had been held valid for these additional interviews could not be included in the earlier lists.
  • To correct this, the Commission has now cancelled the selection list and marks list dated 3 September 2025 and 11 June 2026 with immediate effect and removed them from its website, and has declared this new revised selection list including all 4 affected candidates, based strictly on interview merit.

In short, this 6 July 2026 list supersedes and replaces all previously issued selection and marks lists for this post.

Post and Vacancy Details

The main part (87%) selection list covers 185 posts, distributed as follows:

Category Total Posts Reserved for Women Reserved for MP State Contract Employees
Unreserved (UR) 55 19 28
SC 28 10 14
ST 50 18 25
OBC 24 8 12
EWS 28 10 14
Total 185 - -

Out of the total 208 posts advertised, 12 posts were reserved for persons with disabilities (Orthopedically impaired – 3, Visually impaired – 3, Hearing impaired – 3, Multiple disabilities – 3).

Vacant Posts

As per the Commission's notification, out of the 185 main-part posts, 69 posts (SC – 7, ST – 37, EWS – 25) remain vacant due to non-availability of adequate or eligible candidates. Additionally, out of the 12 posts reserved for persons with disabilities, 11 posts remain vacant due to non-availability of eligible candidates in that category. As per government instructions, an equal number of posts (8, since 3 were already accounted for) from the available unreserved category have also been kept vacant against these disability-category vacancies. In total, 77 posts remain vacant under this selection list.

Selection Stage Covered

This list represents the final selection stage based on merit of interview marks. It is not a written exam result; selection was made purely on the basis of personal interviews conducted on the dates mentioned above, following the earlier document verification and eligibility screening stages.

  • Merit/Selection List: Released (6 July 2026)
  • Marks/Score Card: Not available with this list. The Commission has cancelled the earlier marks lists dated 3 September 2025 and 11 June 2026; a corresponding revised marks list, if issued separately, has not been officially announced in this notification.
  • Cut-Off Marks: Not officially released in this notification.

Important Dates

Event Date

Interviews (Round 1) 3 July 2025
Interviews (Round 2) 11 August 2025 – 12 August 2025

High Court-Directed Additional Interview Notice 13 May 2026
Additional Interviews Conducted 21 May 2026
Revised Selection List (Earlier) 11 June 2026 (Cancelled)
New Revised Selection List 6 July 2026

How to Check the MPPSC Paediatric Specialist Selection List

  1. Visit the official MPPSC website, mppsc.mp.gov.in.
  2. Look for the notification titled "New Revised Selection List – Paediatric Specialist" under the Results/Selection List section.
  3. Open the PDF linked against reference number 4846/52/2024/चयन dated 6 July 2026.
  4. Use Ctrl+F (or the search option on mobile) to locate your roll number/serial number in the Main List or Supplementary List.
  5. Download and save the PDF for future reference.

Details Mentioned on the Selection List

The official PDF released by MPPSC includes the following details for each selected candidate:

  • Serial Number
  • Roll/Enrolment Number
  • Candidate Name
  • Gender
  • Seat Allotted (e.g., UNR, OBC, SC, ST, EWS, and sub-categories such as UNRF for unreserved-female)
  • Category
  • Remarks such as "प्रावधिक" (provisional) or disability category, where applicable

The list is divided into a Main List (108 candidates) and a Supplementary List (13 candidates). As a general practice, we do not reproduce the full roll number/name list in this article; candidates should verify their own name and roll number directly from the official PDF linked below.

What to Do After the Selection List

  • Check your name and roll number carefully in both the Main List and Supplementary List.
  • Keep a downloaded/printed copy of the selection list PDF for your records.
  • Wait for further official communication from MPPSC or the Public Health and Medical Education Department regarding document verification and joining formalities.
  • The Commission has stated that this selection result remains subject to the final outcome of pending cases before the Supreme Court (SLP No. 8764/2023, SLP No. 12398/2023) and the Madhya Pradesh High Court (WP 5901/2019, WP 5596/2024, WP 39631/2025, WP 6180/2026, WP 11075/2026). Selected candidates should keep this in mind.

Documents Required for the Next Stage

The Commission's notification does not specify a document verification schedule or document checklist at this stage. Based on standard MPPSC recruitment practice, candidates are generally advised to keep the following documents ready, though this is not an official list issued with this particular notification:

  • Educational qualification certificates and mark sheets
  • Category certificate (SC/ST/OBC/EWS), if applicable
  • MP domicile certificate, if applicable
  • Experience certificates, if applicable
  • Valid photo ID proof

Note: Document verification dates have not been announced officially in this notification.

Selection Process

As per the Commission's notes, the selection process followed for this recruitment was:

  1. Screening of applications and eligibility of candidates
  2. Personal Interview of eligible candidates
  3. Preparation of merit list strictly on the basis of interview marks

The Commission has clarified that where sufficient women candidates were not available for women-reserved posts, such posts were filled by male candidates of the same category, as per General Administration Department Circular No. 3/2/97/3 dated 10.02.1997. Similarly, for unreserved (open) posts, only those reserved-category candidates who qualified without any relaxation and on pure merit were selected, as per Circular No. F-7-46/99 dated 7 November 2000.

Important Instructions

  • This selection list is a revised list; the earlier selection lists and marks lists dated 3 September 2025 and 11 June 2026 stand cancelled and removed from the MPPSC website with immediate effect.
  • The Commission reserves the right to correct the result if any computer or clerical error comes to its notice after publication.
  • This result covers only the main part (87%) of advertised posts; no separate result for the provisional part (13%) will be issued since no eligible candidates were available for it.
  • A total of 77 posts remain vacant under this list due to non-availability of adequate eligible candidates in certain categories, including disability categories.
  • The selection result is subject to the final decision of pending cases in the Supreme Court and the Madhya Pradesh High Court, as listed above.

Candidates are advised to check the official MPPSC website directly, as third-party links are not being provided here.

How to Check the JPSC CCS Backlog PT Result 2026

Candidates can check the JPSC CCS Backlog PT Result 2026 by following these steps:

  1. Visit the official JPSC website, www.jpsc.gov.in.
  2. Look for the notice titled "Jharkhand Combined Civil Services (Backlog) Preliminary Competitive Examination-2025 (Advt. No. 05/2026) Result".
  3. Open the result PDF link.
  4. Use Ctrl+F (or the search function) to find your roll number in the list.
  5. Download and save the result PDF for future reference.

Details Mentioned on the Result

The official PDF released by JPSC contains the following details:

  • Examination name: Combined Civil Services (Backlog) PT Examination-2025
  • Advertisement number: 05/2026
  • Page-wise list of qualified candidates' roll numbers
  • Signature of the Secretary, Jharkhand Public Service Commission, Ranchi

The result document does not include candidate names, marks, or category-wise breakup only qualifying roll numbers are listed.

What to Do After the Result

Candidates whose roll numbers appear in the qualifying list should immediately proceed with the following:

  • Fill the online application for the Main (Written) Backlog Competitive Examination between 7 July 2026 and 14 July 2026, on the application portal https://jpscotr.com.
  • Select one language and literature subject for Paper II as per the advertisement.
  • Choose either Hindi or English as the medium for answering questions (except the language and literature paper) and for the interview.
  • Indicate service/cadre preference among the three services/cadres mentioned in the advertisement.
  • Upload all required scanned documents in PDF format.
  • Submit a hard copy of the application along with self-attested documents to the JPSC office by 20 July 2026.

Documents Required for the Mains Application

Depending on individual eligibility claims, candidates must upload the following documents while filling the Mains application:

  • Educational qualification certificates supporting the claims made in the application
  • Category certificate for Female, EBC-I, BC-II, SC, or ST candidates, as applicable
  • Local (domicile) certificate for claiming reservation benefits
  • Disability certificate (minimum 40% disability), countersigned by a competent Medical Board and Chief Medical Officer/Medical Superintendent, for PwBD candidates
  • No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the Controlling Officer/Head of Department, for candidates who are regular Jharkhand government employees
  • Relevant documents for candidates claiming maximum age relaxation as Ex-servicemen

Original documents will need to be produced at the time of document verification.

Selection Process

The selection process for the Jharkhand Combined Civil Services (Backlog) Competitive Examination-2025 consists of the following stages:

  1. Preliminary (PT) Examination Result Declared
  2. Main (Written) Examination Scheduled for 1, 2, and 3 August 2026
  3. Interview/Personality Test (as per the detailed advertisement on jpscotr.com)

Important Instructions

  • JPSC reserves the right to correct any error or typographical mistake found in the result at a later stage.
  • Candidates should thoroughly read the detailed advertisement and application instructions on https://jpscotr.com before starting the online application process.

The recruitment was carried out for the post of Assistant Professor, Hindi, under the Higher Education Department, Government of Madhya Pradesh. This recruitment was advertised through Advertisement No. 24/2024 dated 30.12.2024, along with subsequent corrigenda issued from time to time.

The result is officially declared for 87 percent of the advertised posts, which is referred to as the "main part" of the recruitment. The remaining 13 percent, called the "provisional part," has not been declared yet. According to the official notice, the provisional part selection result will be announced after the final judicial decision in the pending court cases related to Other Backward Class (OBC) reservation.

Selection Stage Covered

This result reflects the final selection stage of the recruitment process. It is based on the cumulative merit of marks obtained in both the written examination and the interview.

Candidates who appeared for the CBO online examination on 14 March 2026 can check their roll number or registration number in the result PDF to confirm their selection for the next stage the interview round.

This article covers everything you need to know about the SBI CBO Result 2026, including the direct download link, step-by-step checking process, vacancy breakup, selection process, and the interview schedule.

SBI CBO Result 2026 - Key Highlights

Before downloading the PDF, candidates should quickly review the core details of the SBI CBO 2026 recruitment cycle summarised in the table below.

Recruiting Body State Bank of India (SBI)

SBI CBO Result 2026 Direct Download Link

This section gives you quick access to the official SBI CBO Result PDF so you don't have to navigate through multiple pages on the SBI website.

The list of candidates qualified for the interview has been uploaded as a PDF on the SBI careers page. You can access the result PDF directly here:

SBI CBO Result 2026 PDF - Direct Download Link

The PDF lists roll numbers/registration numbers of candidates shortlisted for the interview, along with the advertisement number and post details.

How to Check SBI CBO Result 2026 (Step-by-Step)

If the direct link isn't working due to heavy traffic, candidates can also check the result by navigating the official SBI careers website manually using the steps below.

  1. Visit the official SBI careers portal at sbi.bank.in.
  2. Click on the "Current Openings" section on the homepage.
  3. Look for the link titled "Recruitment of Circle Based Officer (List of Candidates Qualified for Interview Announced)".
  4. Click on "List of Candidates Qualified for Interview".
  5. The result PDF will open download and save it.
  6. Use Ctrl + F to search your roll number or registration number quickly within the PDF.

SBI CBO Result 2026: What Does the PDF Contain?

Candidates should know exactly what information appears in the result document before they search for their names, so they can verify their status correctly.

The SBI CBO Result 2026 PDF includes:

  • Recruiting authority's name and advertisement number
  • Post name (Circle Based Officer)
  • Roll numbers/registration numbers of candidates shortlisted for interview
  • Instructions regarding the next stage of recruitment

There is no separate merit list at this stage the PDF is a qualifying list for the interview round, not a final selection list.

SBI CBO 2026 Total Vacancies

Knowing the total number of vacancies helps candidates understand how competitive the shortlisting for interview has been.

The official SBI notification and the state-wise vacancy breakup add up to 2,050 posts. It's worth noting for accuracy that a few report portals have listed the vacancy figure as 2,273; candidates are advised to cross-check the exact number against the official CBO notification PDF on sbi.co.in, since this is the only authoritative source for the final vacancy count.

SBI CBO Selection Process 2026: What Happens After the Result?

Candidates naturally want to know what comes next after clearing the online exam this section outlines the complete selection journey.

Shortlisted candidates will now move through the remaining stages of the SBI CBO recruitment process:

  • Interview
  • Language Proficiency Test
  • Document Verification
  • Medical Examination
  • Final Selection

The final merit list is prepared based on combined performance in the online examination and interview, with a reported weightage split of 75:25 (online test : interview), and the interview itself carries 50 marks.

SBI CBO Interview 2026: Date and Details

Since the interview is the immediate next step for shortlisted candidates, here's what is currently known about its schedule.

Reports indicate the SBI CBO interview round is scheduled for mid-July 2026, with different sources citing dates of 13 July and 14 July 2026. As this detail is subject to confirmation, candidates should wait for the official interview call letter on the SBI careers portal for their exact date, time, and venue rather than relying on any single unconfirmed date.

How Is the SBI CBO Merit Calculated?

Understanding the marking scheme helps candidates interpret their own performance realistically before the scorecard is released.

The SBI CBO written exam follows a standard negative marking pattern:

Final Marks = (Correct Answers × 1) - (Wrong Answers × 0.25)

Answer Type Marking Rule
Correct Answer +1 mark
Wrong Answer -0.25 mark
Unattempted Question No penalty

A separate scorecard showing section-wise and overall marks is typically released by SBI after the result, accessible through candidate login credentials on the careers portal.

IBPS RRB Clerk Reserve List 2026 Out - Check Provisional Allotment (CRP XIV)

The Institute of Banking Personnel Selection (IBPS) released the IBPS RRB Clerk Reserve List 2026 on 30th June 2026 for candidates who appeared in the CRP RRBs-XIV recruitment cycle. Candidates who were not allotted a bank in the main result can now log in to the official IBPS portal with their registration number and password/date of birth to check their provisional allotment status under the reserve list. The list currently covers 26 participating Regional Rural Banks (RRBs), and shortlisted candidates will also be informed through email and SMS on their registered contact details.

Add FJA on  As Preferred Source

What Is the IBPS RRB Clerk Reserve List 2026?

This section explains the purpose of the reserve list and why IBPS issues it after the main selection round.

A reserve list is a backup panel that IBPS prepares after declaring the final result of the CRP RRBs-XIV exam. Once the primary list of selected candidates is allotted to participating banks, some vacancies remain unfilled because certain selected candidates do not join within the deadline, resign shortly after joining, or get rejected at the document verification stage. To ensure every sanctioned post is filled, IBPS draws candidates from the reserve panel, based on merit, category, and the number of vacancies still open, and provisionally allots them to a Regional Rural Bank for the Office Assistant/Customer Service Associate (Clerk) post.

IBPS RRB Clerk Reserve List 2026 - Quick Overview

This table summarizes the key details of the reserve list release for a quick reference before you check your status.

Particulars Details
Conducting Body Institute of Banking Personnel Selection (IBPS)
Exam Name CRP RRBs-XIV (Clerk/Office Assistant)
Post Customer Service Associate (CSA) / Clerk
List Type 1st Reserve List (Provisional Allotment)
Release Date 30th June 2026
Participating Banks Covered 26 RRBs
Mode of Allotment Online, login-based
Allotment Status Provisional (subject to verification)

IBPS RRB Clerk Reserve List 2026: Direct Link to Check

This section gives you the official login link to view your provisional allotment status under the reserve list.

Candidates who appeared in the IBPS RRB Clerk Mains exam but did not feature in the original selection list can check their status through the official IBPS portal. Login requires your Registration Number/Roll Number and Password/Date of Birth.

IBPS RRB Clerk Reserve List 2026 Login Link (Active)

How to Check IBPS RRB Clerk Reserve List 2026 Online?

This section outlines the step-by-step process to view and download your reserve list allotment status.

  1. Visit the official IBPS website at ibps.in.
  2. Click on the "CRP-CSA (Customer Service Associate)" tab on the homepage.
  3. Select "CRP-CRP XIV – Provisional Allotment under Reserve List."
  4. Enter your Registration Number/Roll Number and Password/Date of Birth.
  5. Fill in the captcha code and click on the Login button.
  6. View your allotment status and download the result for future reference.

How Will You Know If You're Selected?

This section explains how IBPS notifies candidates who get provisional allotment through the reserve list.

Candidates who are provisionally allotted a bank through the reserve list will receive an official communication via email and SMS on their registered email ID and mobile number. It is advisable to regularly check your registered contact details and the official IBPS portal so you don't miss any update.

What Happens After the Reserve List Allotment?

This section explains the next stages candidates must complete after receiving a provisional allotment.

Getting your name on the reserve list does not mean final selection it is a provisional allotment that becomes confirmed only after the bank completes verification. The typical process that follows includes:

  • Document Verification: Submission of original certificates and identity proofs for cross-checking.
  • Submission of Required Certificates: Educational, category, and other eligibility-related documents as specified by the allotted bank.
  • Medical Examination: Some banks may require a fitness check before final confirmation.
  • Joining Formalities: Completion of paperwork and reporting to the allotted branch.
  • Induction/Training Process: Orientation and training conducted by the bank before you begin regular duties.

Candidates should keep all original and photocopied documents ready in advance to avoid last-minute issues during verification.

Why Does IBPS Release a Reserve List?

This section explains the broader purpose behind the reserve list mechanism in IBPS recruitment.

A reserve list helps maintain smooth recruitment by ensuring sanctioned vacancies don't remain vacant. It benefits candidates who narrowly missed the initial cut-off by giving them another opportunity, while also helping banks manage manpower requirements efficiently across states and categories.

How to Check RBI Grade B Phase 1 Result 2026 - Step-by-Step Guide

Candidates who are unsure about how to access the RBI Grade B Result 2026 online can follow these simple steps to download the result PDF from the official website of the Reserve Bank of India.

  1. Visit the official website of the Reserve Bank of India at rbi.org.in
  2. Scroll to the bottom of the homepage and click on the "Opportunities@RBI" link

About RBI Grade B Recruitment 2026

The Reserve Bank of India issued the RBI Grade B 2026 recruitment notification for 60 Officer posts across three cadres General, DEPR (Department of Economic and Policy Research), and DSIM (Department of Statistics and Information Management). The selection process is conducted in three stages: Phase 1 (Prelims), Phase 2 (Mains), and Interview. Candidates who clear all stages are offered posting as Officers in Grade 'B' on probation.

RBI Grade B Selection Process 2026

Understanding the full selection process helps candidates plan their preparation for the upcoming Phase 2 exam. The RBI Grade B selection is conducted in three sequential stages as outlined below.

Stage Details
Phase 1 (Prelims) Objective Type - Held on 13-14 June 2026
Phase 2 (Mains) Descriptive + Objective - Scheduled 25-26 July 2026
Interview Final round for candidates qualifying Phase 2
  • Phase 1 tests candidates on General Awareness, English Language, Quantitative Aptitude, and Reasoning
  • Phase 2 (Mains) consists of Paper I (General/Finance/Management - Objective & Descriptive) and Paper II & III (Specialised - for DEPR/DSIM)
  • The cut-off marks for Phase 2 will be released along with the RBI Grade B Score Card 2026

What's Next After RBI Grade B Phase 1 Result 2026?

Candidates whose roll numbers appear in the Phase 1 result PDF must now prepare for the RBI Grade B Phase 2 Mains Examination, scheduled for 25th and 26th July 2026. Here is what qualified candidates should do immediately:

  • Download and save the result PDF from the official website
  • Verify your roll number in the qualified candidates list using Ctrl+F
  • Begin focused preparation for Phase 2 Mains Economic and Social Issues, Finance and Management, English (Writing Skills)
  • Stay updated on the Phase 2 Admit Card release on rbi.org.in
  • The RBI Grade B Score Card 2026 with individual marks and cut-off details will be released separately

RBI Grade B Cut Off 2026

The official cut-off marks for Phase 1 have not been separately released as a category-wise table the result is in roll number PDF format only. The Phase 2 cut-off will be declared along with the score card after mains. Candidates can refer to previous years' cut-off trends for an approximate benchmark while preparing for Phase 2.

  5. Final Appointment - Subject to clearing all stages.

Candidates who fail to clear the LPT will be disqualified from the recruitment process even if they have passed the online test. Candidates are advised to keep checking the official RBI website for notices regarding dates and venues for the Language Proficiency Test.

Eligibility Criteria

Candidates must meet the educational qualification, age limit, and nationality conditions set by the Central Bank of India to be eligible for the Apprentice post.

Educational Qualification

  • A graduation degree (bachelor's degree) in any discipline from a recognised university or institute.
  • Candidates should have completed graduation on or after 1 January 2022 (some sources indicate the cut-off as 1 January 2021; candidates should verify the exact date on the official notification).
  • Candidates with one year or more of work or training experience after graduation are not eligible, since this scheme is meant for fresh graduates.
  • Candidates who have already completed apprenticeship training, or are currently undergoing apprenticeship training elsewhere, are not eligible.
  • Basic computer knowledge is required.
  • Candidates must be proficient in the local language of the state they are applying for.

Age Limit

Candidates must be between 20 and 28 years of age as on 31 May 2026, meaning they should be born between 31 May 1998 and 31 May 2006 (both dates inclusive).

Salary / Stipend Details

Selected apprentices will receive a fixed monthly stipend of ₹15,000 during the 12-month training period. Selection Process

The Central Bank of India Apprentice selection process involves two stages:

  1. Online Written Examination: An objective-type computer-based test with no negative marking for wrong answers.
  2. Local Language Proficiency Test: Candidates who qualify the online exam may need to appear for a test assessing reading, writing, and speaking skills in the local language of the applied state. Candidates who studied the local language at Class 10 or Class 12 level may be exempted from this test, subject to document verification.

Final selection also depends on document verification and meeting the required medical fitness standards set by the bank.

  • The question paper is available in English and Hindi, except for the General English section.

What to Carry on Exam Day

Carrying the right documents is essential, as candidates without a valid admit card or ID proof may be denied entry to the exam centre. This checklist covers what you must bring.

  • A clear, printed copy of the BOB Apprentice Admit Card 2026
  • A valid original photo ID proof (such as Aadhaar Card or PAN Card) the same ID used during the application process
  • A recent passport-size photograph
  • Arrive at the exam centre well before the reporting time mentioned on the admit card

What Happens After the Exam?

This section outlines the next stages of the selection process so candidates know what to expect once the online exam is over.

The Bank of Baroda Apprentice selection process does not end with the written exam. Candidates who qualify in the online test move to the following stages:

  1. Document Verification - Shortlisted candidates must produce original documents for eligibility verification.
  2. Language Proficiency Test - Candidates must demonstrate proficiency in the official local language of the state they applied for.
  3. Medical Examination - A final medical fitness check is conducted before confirmation of selection.

Selected apprentices will be engaged for a one-year apprenticeship period and will receive a stipend of ₹15,000 per month during this engagement.

Eligibility Criteria for CSC Aadhaar Operator Recruitment 2026

Candidates planning to apply for the CSC Aadhaar Supervisor Operator Bharti 2026 must meet all eligibility conditions set by CSC e-Governance Services India Ltd. The minimum age requirement is 18 years, and no upper age limit is mentioned in the official notification. Candidates must hold a valid Aadhaar Operator/Supervisor certificate from a UIDAI-authorized testing and certifying agency.

Educational Qualification

Qualification Option Details
Option 1 12th Pass (Intermediate / Senior Secondary)

Age Limit

The minimum age to apply for the CSC Aadhaar Operator Vacancy 2026 is 18 years. No maximum age or age relaxation details are mentioned in the official notification.

Mandatory Certificate Requirement

Every applicant must possess an Aadhaar Operator/Supervisor certificate issued by a Testing & Certifying Agency authorized by UIDAI for delivering Aadhaar services. Additionally, candidates must have basic computer skills. Candidates who do not yet hold this certificate can appear for the Aadhaar Supervisor exam through the link: https://uidai.dexitglobalexams.com/UIDAI/LoginAction.action

Who is NOT Eligible

Salary / Remuneration – CSC Aadhaar Supervisor Operator 2026

Selected candidates under the CSC Aadhaar Operator Recruitment 2026 will be paid as per the state government's prescribed wage structure. The remuneration for all selected Aadhaar Supervisor/Operator candidates will be the minimum wages of the respective state set for semi-skilled manpower. The exact figure will vary from state to state based on the applicable minimum wage notification of Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, or Maharashtra.

How to Obtain the Aadhaar Supervisor Certificate Before Applying

Candidates who do not yet hold the mandatory Aadhaar Operator/Supervisor certificate need to complete two steps before they are eligible to apply for CSC Aadhaar Seva Kendra jobs. First, they must apply for and pass the Aadhaar Supervisor exam; second, they must complete the LMS certification. Both processes are managed through official UIDAI platforms.

  1. Visit the Aadhaar Supervisor exam portal at https://uidai.dexitglobalexams.com/UIDAI/LoginAction.action and submit your exam application.
  2. An authorization request will be sent to the State Team. Once approved, you will be permitted to appear for the Aadhaar Supervisor exam.
  3. After your LMS ID and Password are created and approved, appear for the Aadhaar LMS Certification through the portal at https://e-learning.uidai.gov.in
  4. Once certified, proceed to apply for the CSC Aadhaar Operator/Supervisor district post on the CSC Job Portal.

How to Apply for CSC Aadhaar Supervisor Operator Recruitment 2026

The CSC Aadhaar Operator Apply Online 2026 process is conducted entirely through the official CSC Job Portal at career.csccloud.in. Candidates must ensure they have their Aadhaar Operator/Supervisor certificate ready before beginning the application. The last date to apply is 20 August 2026, and no offline applications are accepted under this recruitment.

  1. Visit the official CSC Job Portal at career.csccloud.in.
  2. Navigate to the relevant job post for your state – Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, or Maharashtra.
  3. Click on the "Apply Now" button on the job post page.
  4. Fill in the online application form with your personal, educational, and certification details.
  5. Upload the required documents including your Aadhaar Operator/Supervisor certificate.
  6. Submit the application form before 20 August 2026.

CSC Aadhaar Supervisor Operator Apply Online 2026

Eligible candidates can submit their online applications for the CSC Aadhaar Seva Kendra Recruitment 2026 through the official CSC Job Portal. The apply online facility is available for all four states – Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, and Maharashtra. Ensure your Aadhaar Operator/Supervisor certificate is valid and issued by a UIDAI-authorized agency before clicking Apply Now. The online application window closes on 20 August 2026.

State Apply Online Link

Chhattisgarh Apply Now – Chhattisgarh

Common Mistakes to Avoid in CSC Aadhaar Operator Recruitment 2026

Many candidates make avoidable errors while applying for the CSC Aadhaar Supervisor Operator Vacancy 2026 that can lead to rejection of their application. The points below are based on common patterns seen in similar contractual government recruitment drives and are not derived from the official notification.

  1. Applying without a valid UIDAI certificate: The Aadhaar Operator/Supervisor certificate from a UIDAI-authorized agency is a mandatory requirement. Applying without it will result in disqualification.
  2. VLEs applying despite ineligibility: VLEs are explicitly barred from applying. Submitting an application as a VLE wastes your time and will be rejected at the verification stage.
  3. Applying for the wrong district: Each vacancy is district-specific. Ensure you apply for the correct district as per your location and preference.
  4. Incomplete LMS Certification: Candidates sometimes have the Supervisor exam cleared but not the LMS Certification. Both are required before applying.
  5. Submitting incorrect documents: Upload clear, legible scans of your educational certificates and Aadhaar Operator certificate. Blurry or mismatched documents can cause rejection.
  6. Missing the last date: The portal closes applications on 20 August 2026. Do not wait until the last day — technical issues near the deadline are common.
  7. Confusing CSC e-Governance with state government jobs: This is a contractual, not permanent government post. Ensure you understand the terms of engagement before applying.

IOB Apprentice Recruitment 2026-27 Eligibility Criteria

Candidates applying for IOB Apprentice Recruitment 2026-27 must be Citizens of India. Merely applying, being shortlisted, or appearing for document verification and personal interaction does not guarantee an offer of engagement in the Bank.

Educational Qualification

Candidates must hold a Degree (Graduation) in any discipline from a University recognized by the Government of India, or an equivalent qualification recognized by the Central Government. The result must be declared on or before 31.07.2026. Candidates registered under the National Apprenticeship Training Scheme (NATS) must have had their graduation result declared between 01.03.2022 and 31.07.2026, both dates inclusive, and must produce mark sheets and provisional or degree certificates when required.

Age Limit

The minimum age is 20 years and the maximum age is 28 years as on the cut-off date of 01.07.2026 for General and EWS category candidates, meaning the date of birth should fall between 01.07.1998 and 01.07.2006, both dates inclusive. Candidates registered under NAPS should be less than 34 years as on the cut-off date, after applicable relaxation.

Category Age Relaxation
Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe 5 years
Other Backward Classes (Non-Creamy Layer) 3 years
Persons with Benchmark Disabilities 10 years

Age relaxation for SC/ST/OBC candidates is allowed on a cumulative basis with only one of the remaining categories of relaxation. To claim age relaxation, candidates must submit the requisite certificate at the time of personal interaction along with original certificates.

Semi-Urban/Rural 7,850 (14,000 minus 6,150 Government subsidy)

The Government share of Rs. 6,150 will be directly credited to the apprentice's bank account through DBT mode. Apprentices are not eligible for any other allowances or benefits.

IOB Apprentice Application Fee 2026-27

The application fee for IOB Apprentice Recruitment 2026-27 must be paid online between 07.07.2026 and 22.07.2026 through the BEEP portal only. The fee is non-refundable and cannot be adjusted against any other engagement process.

IOB Apprentice Selection Process 2026-27

Selection for IOB Apprentice Recruitment 2026-27 will be based on an online examination, a test of the local language wherever applicable, and personal interaction if decided by the Bank. Satisfying the eligibility criteria alone does not guarantee a call for the online examination.

Online Written Examination Pattern

Test Name Number of Questions Marks
General/Financial Awareness 25 25
General English 25 25
Quantitative and Reasoning Aptitude 25 25
Computer or Subject Knowledge 25 25
Total 100 100

The total duration of the examination is 90 minutes. The examination will be conducted online using the candidate's own front camera-enabled desktop, laptop, tablet, or smartphone, and candidates must display the same ID proof uploaded on the apprenticeship portal. Candidates must score a minimum aggregate percentage as decided by the Bank, with a 5 percent relaxation available for SC/ST/OBC/PwBD candidates. There is no minimum qualifying mark for individual subjects.

Test of Local Language

Candidates applying for a particular state must be proficient in reading, writing, speaking, and understanding at least one local language of that state. This test is conducted during document verification after qualifying the written examination. Candidates who have studied the specified local language up to 10th or 12th standard are exempted from this test.

Wait-list

A state-category-wise waitlist will be maintained for one year from the date of the result or the next engagement exercise, whichever is earlier.

Documents Required for IOB Apprentice Document Verification

Candidates shortlisted for document verification or personal interaction must produce the following documents in original along with self-attested photocopies.

  • Printout of the valid communication for personal interaction or reporting
  • Printout of the email from BFSI SSC containing submitted application data
  • Proof of date of birth (birth certificate or SSLC/Std. X certificate with DOB)
  • Photo identity proof such as Passport, Aadhaar/e-Aadhaar, PAN Card, Driving Licence, or Voter's Card
  • Consolidated mark sheets and relevant educational qualification certificates
  • Caste certificate in the prescribed format for SC/ST/OBC/EWS candidates
  • Non-creamy layer OBC certificate issued on or after 01.04.2026, where applicable
  • Disability certificate in the prescribed format for PwBD candidates
  • Any other relevant documents supporting eligibility

How to Apply for IOB Apprentice Recruitment 2026-27

Candidates can apply online for IOB Apprentice Recruitment 2026-27 from 07.07.2026 to 20.07.2026 by following the steps below.

  1. Register on the NATS portal at https://nats.education.gov.in or the NAPS portal at https://www.apprenticeshipindia.gov.in before applying.
  2. Visit the "Career Opportunities" page on www.bfsissc.com or https://beep.bfsissc.com.
  3. NATS-registered candidates should log in at https://nats.education.gov.in/student_type.php and apply under "Apply against advertised vacancies" for Indian Overseas Bank.
  4. NAPS-registered candidates should visit https://www.apprenticeshipindia.gov.in/apprenticeship/opportunity, search "Indian Overseas Bank," click "View," and then "Apply for this Opportunity."
  5. Provide the NATS/NAPS enrolment number while filling the online application form.
  6. Apply for engagement from only one State/UT, preferably the home State/UT.
  7. Pay the requisite application fee/intimation charges online between 07.07.2026 and 22.07.2026.

No other mode of application or payment will be accepted. Applications once submitted cannot be withdrawn, and fees once paid will not be refunded under any circumstances.

Important Instructions for IOB Apprentice Recruitment 2026-27

  • Candidates should not have undergone apprenticeship earlier with IOB or any other organization, or been terminated from apprenticeship training due to their own fault.
  • Candidates with one year or more of training or job experience after completing the educational qualification are not eligible.
  • Apprentices are not treated as "employees" of the Bank and are not entitled to employee benefits.
  • Apprentices are entitled to one day of casual leave per month, totaling 12 days per year, with a maximum of 4 days availed at a time.
  • No Ex-servicemen or Disabled Ex-servicemen shall be engaged as apprentices, and there is no reservation for them in this process.
  • The Bank has no obligation to offer regular employment during or after the apprenticeship period.
  • Furnishing false, incorrect, or tampered information will lead to disqualification or termination, even after engagement.
  • Any request for change of address, email ID, or document verification dates will not be entertained.
  • Any dispute arising out of this recruitment is subject to the sole jurisdiction of courts situated at Chennai.

  • The engagement is purely on a contractual basis.
  • Associates have the legal status of an independent consultant vis-à-vis NHIDCL and shall not be regarded, for any purpose, as a staff member, official, or employee of NHIDCL. Nothing in the individual consultancy contracts or these guidelines establishes an employer-employee or principal-agent relationship between NHIDCL and the Associates.
  • Associates will be engaged for a fixed period of 2 (two) years, which may be extended by 1 (one) year at a time up to a maximum tenure of 3 (three) years, i.e., 2+1 years, for providing high-quality services on specific projects as per the requirement of the verticals/divisions. Continuation beyond the first and subsequent years is contingent on the decision of the Consultants’ Review Committee (CRC).

Terms of Reference (Role & Responsibilities)

The Terms of Reference (ToR) include the outputs to be delivered and the functions to be performed, which shall be specific, measurable, attainable, results-based, and time-bound. An indicative ToR for Associates (SSGS) is as follows; detailed ToR will be drawn up by the respective Regional Offices of NHIDCL for which Associates are selected, and this ToR is deemed part of the contract.

  • Project Preparation & Design Appraisal: Assist in the review of feasibility studies, DPRs, alignment plans, and compliance with IRC/MoRTH standards.
  • Construction Supervision & Project Monitoring: Undertake field visits, monitor physical/financial progress, and report on quality, safety, and adherence to specifications.
  • Contract & Documentation Support: Assist in contract management, correspondence, technical notes, and maintenance of project records/MIS.
  • Quality Assurance & Technical Compliance: Review test results, site practices, and ensure compliance with approved drawings and Quality Assurance Plans (QAPs).
  • Post-Construction & O&M Support: Support completion documentation, punch-list closure, and monitoring during the defect liability period.

Induction & Payment

  • There will be an Induction Module of 3 (three) days, which each hired Associate must go through.
  • The Competent Authority may prescribe "Competency Tests" at any time, periodic or otherwise, and Associates are expected to clear these as per the minimum qualifying marks prescribed.
  • All engagements are subject to the successful completion of a Background Verification (BGV) process, which may include verification of the candidate's identity, address, educational and professional qualifications, character antecedents, and any other information deemed necessary by NHIDCL. If the outcome of the BGV is found unsatisfactory at any point – before or after appointment – NHIDCL reserves the right to withdraw or cancel the engagement.

Selection Process

The Hiring Notice directs eligible candidates to apply through the NHIDCL Resource Pool Portal; the notice does not detail a separate written test, and selection proceeds through NHIDCL shortlisting candidates from the Eligible Pool of Applicants for interview, assessment, or other stages, as decided by the Competent Authority based on vacancy availability and operational requirements.

  • For the purpose of this Hiring Notice, the "Eligible Pool of Applicants" means candidates whose applications/profiles for the relevant position are available in the NHIDCL Resource Pool Portal and who satisfy the prescribed educational qualifications, domicile requirements, age criteria, and other eligibility conditions applicable to the position.
  • Candidates who applied for the same position under Hiring Notice No. 05/2025, and whose applications are available in the Resource Pool Portal, need not apply again. Further, candidates who were shortlisted and called for interview pursuant to Hiring Notice No. 05/2025 but were not selected shall also remain eligible for consideration and need not submit a fresh application, subject to their continued inclusion in the Eligible Pool of Applicants and fulfilment of the eligibility conditions prescribed in this Recruitment Notice.
  • NHIDCL may, at its discretion and subject to availability of vacancies, operational requirements, and approval of the Competent Authority, consider, shortlist, and call candidates from the Eligible Pool of Applicants for interview, assessment, or any other stage of selection for present or future requirements under the Scheme – either pursuant to a Recruitment Notice or without issuance of a separate public advertisement, where deemed appropriate.
  • Registration in the Resource Pool Portal or inclusion in the Eligible Pool of Applicants does not confer any right to shortlisting, interview, engagement, or appointment.

How to Apply Online for NHIDCL Associate Recruitment 2026

Eligible candidates may apply through the NHIDCL Resource Pool Portal.

  1. Visit the Resource Pool Portal – Go to Apply Here.
  2. Register/Update Profile – Register yourself and submit your application/profile for the relevant position and State/UT, ensuring you meet the domicile, qualification, and age criteria for that position.
  3. Submit Within the Window – Applications must be submitted between 8 July 2026, 10:00 AM, and 5 August 2026, 5:00 PM.

Interested candidates may register themselves on the Resource Pool Portal and update their profile at any time during the year, even if the last date of application for a particular advertisement has already passed. NHIDCL may also issue abridged advertisements directing prospective candidates to register and submit their profiles through the Resource Pool Portal for future requirements.

All correspondence shall be made only via email at [email protected]. Any other mode of correspondence shall not be valid.

Important Instructions

  • Candidates must ensure they meet all eligibility criteria and possess essential qualification recognized by AICTE/UGC/State Technical Boards.
  • Furnishing inaccurate, wrong, incomplete, or misleading information may lead to rejection of the candidature.
  • Candidates must keep their email ID active for one year; no change in the email ID would be allowed.
  • Corrigendum, addendum, or errata will be posted only on NHIDCL's website at www.nhidcl.com, under the heading "Resource Portal".
  • Canvassing or external influence will disqualify the candidate from selection.
  • Candidates should avoid middlemen, recruitment agents/consultants, and fraudulent job promises.
  • All disputes are subject to Delhi High Court jurisdiction, with the English version prevailing for interpretation.
  • Personal information collected during the verification process shall be handled in accordance with applicable laws, rules, and NHIDCL's policies, and used only for the purpose of assessment and verification relevant to the engagement.
  • For General Terms and Conditions of Engagement, candidates should refer to Section 5 of the Scheme for Young Professionals, Expert Professionals, and Empanelment of Persons of Eminence. Provisions of the Scheme shall apply and supersede any contradictory instructions in this Recruitment Notice.

IBPS CRP SPL-XVI Eligibility Criteria 2026

For posts other than IT Officer, candidates must also have studied Computer/Information Technology as a subject in High School, College, or Institute, or hold a certificate/diploma/degree in computer operations.

Payment can be made using Debit Cards (RuPay/Visa/MasterCard/Maestro), Credit Cards, Internet Banking, IMPS, Cash Cards, Mobile Wallets, or UPI.

IBPS Specialist Officer Selection Process 2026

Selection under IBPS CRP SPL-XVI 2026 follows a three-stage process: Online Preliminary Examination, Online Main Examination, and a Common Interview. Only candidates who clear each stage progress to the next, and the final merit list is based on Main Examination and Interview scores combined.

  1. Online Preliminary Examination – Tentatively in August 2026; candidates must clear individual cut-offs in each of four tests.
  2. Preliminary Result – Declared in September/October 2026.
  3. Online Main Examination – Tentatively in November 2026; scores from this stage alone are used for interview shortlisting and final merit.
  4. Main Exam Result – Declared in November 2026.
  5. Common Interview – Conducted by Participating Banks and coordinated by Nodal Banks in November/December 2026; total 100 marks with minimum qualifying marks of 40% (35% for SC/ST/OBC/PwBD).
  6. Provisional Allotment – Expected in January 2027, based on merit-cum-preference with an 80:20 weightage between Main Exam and Interview.

Exam Pattern Overview

The Preliminary Exam for IT Officer, Agricultural Field Officer, HR/Personnel Officer, and Marketing Officer consists of 100 questions for 125 marks across English Language, Reasoning, Quantitative Aptitude, and Professional Knowledge, to be completed in 80 minutes. The Main Exam for the same posts carries 150 objective questions for 200 marks plus a Descriptive Paper of 25 marks, totaling 225 marks in 155 minutes. Law Officer and Rajbhasha Adhikari have a similar structure but include General Awareness with Special Reference to Banking Industry in place of Quantitative Aptitude.

There is a penalty of 0.25 marks for each wrong answer in objective tests; no penalty applies for unattempted questions.

IBPS CRP SPL-XVI Apply Online 2026

Candidates can apply for IBPS Specialist Officer Recruitment 2026 only through the online mode on the official IBPS website; no other application method is accepted. The steps below outline the complete registration and payment process.

  1. Visit the official website www.ibps.in and click on the "CRP SPL" link on the homepage.
  2. Select "Click Here to Apply Online for CRP-Specialist Officers (CRP SPL-XVI)" to open the application form.
  3. Click "Click Here for New Registration" and enter basic details to generate a Provisional Registration Number and Password.
  4. Log in again using the provisional credentials to complete the application form.
  5. Upload photograph, signature, left thumb impression, handwritten declaration, and SSC/SSLC/10th standard certificate as per specifications.
  6. Capture and upload a live photograph via webcam or mobile phone.
  7. Verify all details carefully, since no changes are allowed after clicking "Complete Registration" (except during the 2-day Edit Window).
  8. Pay the applicable application fee online via Debit Card, Credit Card, Net Banking, or UPI.
  9. Download and print the system-generated application form and e-receipt for future reference.

IBPS Specialist Officer Salary and Pay Scale 2026

Selected candidates under IBPS CRP SPL-XVI will be appointed as Specialist Officers, Scale I, with pay determined by the standard officer pay scale applicable across Participating Banks. Officials are also eligible for allowances and perquisites as per each bank's applicable rules.

IBPS CRP SPL-XVI Document Requirements

Shortlisted candidates must produce original documents along with self-attested photocopies at the time of interview, failing which their candidature can be cancelled. Required documents include the interview call letter, system-generated application printout, proof of date of birth, photo identity proof, educational mark sheets/certificates, and category certificates (SC/ST/OBC-NCL/EWS/PwBD) as applicable, all in prescribed Government of India formats.

OBC candidates must submit a Non-Creamy Layer certificate issued on or after 01.04.2026, while EWS candidates need an Income & Asset Certificate valid for the year 2026-27 for financial year 2025-26.

Common Mistakes to Avoid While Applying for IBPS CRP SPL-XVI

Many candidates lose their chance at IBPS Specialist Officer Recruitment 2026 due to avoidable errors during the application process. Being aware of these common mistakes in advance can help ensure a smooth, error-free submission.

  • Applying for multiple posts: A candidate can apply for only one post; multiple applications are summarily rejected.
  • Uploading incorrect photo/signature size: Photos must be 4.5cm × 3.5cm (20-50 KB), and signatures 10-20 KB; oversized or blurred files cause application rejection.
  • Writing the declaration in capital letters: The handwritten declaration must be in the candidate's own handwriting, in English, and NOT in capital letters.
  • Ignoring the Edit Window: Since most fields like Name, Email ID, Mobile Number, and Nationality cannot be edited after submission, double-check all entries before final submission.
  • Missing the fee payment deadline: Applying without completing fee payment within 01.07.2026 to 21.07.2026 renders the form incomplete and invalid.
  • Not retaining photograph copies: Candidates should keep at least 8 copies of the uploaded photograph, as these are required at multiple stages including exam day.

SSC ASO Exam Pattern 2026 – Scheme of Examination

The SSC Assistant Section Officer Exam 2026 is conducted in two parts. Part-I is a Computer Based Examination (CBE) carrying 300 marks, and Part-II involves Evaluation of Service Records (APARs) carrying 100 marks. The final merit is prepared on the combined aggregate of both parts. There is no separate qualifying exam - this is a competitive examination.

Part-I: Computer Based Examination (300 Marks)

Paper Subjects Type Max. Marks Duration
Paper-I (i) General Awareness – flagship programmes and GoI initiatives
(ii) Constitutional provisions and their general application in GoI
(iii) Parliamentary procedures (Manual of Parliamentary Procedures, MoPA instructions)
(iv) Reading Comprehension in English / Hindi
(v) Central Secretariat – Manual of Office Procedure
(vi) Allocation of Business Rules and Transaction of Business Rules
(vii) Noting and Drafting		 Objective (MCQ) 150 3 hours (4 hours for eligible scribe candidates)
Paper-II (i) Service Rules – Leave Rules, Conduct & CCA Rules, Pension and NPS Rules
(ii) Financial Rules – TA, LTC
(iii) Legislations – RTI Act 2005, POSH Act 2013
(iv) Records Management
(v) Précis Writing		 Objective (MCQ) 150 3 hours (4 hours for eligible scribe candidates)

There is a negative marking of 0.25 marks (25%) for each wrong answer in both Paper-I and Paper-II. Candidates must attempt the examination only in the language (English or Hindi) opted in the application form. There will be no question paper in Braille.

Part-II: Evaluation of Record of Service (100 Marks)

One hundred marks are reserved for evaluation of Annual Performance Appraisal Reports (APARs). Candidates shortlisted based on their Part-I aggregate performance will proceed to Part-II. Marks from Part-II will be added to determine the final rank. Once APARs have been evaluated, no request for change in APAR grading will be entertained.

SSC ASO Selection Process 2026

The SSC ASO selection process 2026 is a two-stage merit-based system. Candidates must clear the Computer Based Examination before their service records are evaluated. Final selection is strictly based on combined merit - no candidate has a right to selection merely by passing the exam.

  1. Stage 1 – Computer Based Examination (Part-I): Paper-I and Paper-II, each of 150 marks. The Commission may fix minimum qualifying marks individually for each paper.
  2. Stage 2 – APAR Evaluation (Part-II): Only candidates who qualify Part-I are eligible. Service records (APARs) are evaluated for 100 marks.
  3. Final Merit: Aggregate of Part-I (300 marks) + Part-II (100 marks) = 400 marks total. Names of finally selected candidates will be arranged in order of merit separately for each cadre.

Tie-Breaking Rules

In case of equal aggregate marks, ties are resolved in the following order: (i) Marks in Paper-I, (ii) Marks in Paper-II, (iii) Date of birth - older candidate ranked higher, (iv) Alphabetical order of names.

Pay Scale – SSC ASO Salary 2026

Candidates wondering about the salary for Assistant Section Officer will be pleased to know that this is a Group B Non-Gazetted post. The SSC ASO pay scale is at Pay Level-7 in the 7th Pay Commission Pay Matrix, with a pay range of Rs. 44,900 to Rs. 1,42,400 per month. Additional allowances such as HRA, DA, and TA apply as per government rules.

Scribe and Compensatory Time Provisions

PwBD candidates in the category of Blindness and Cerebral Palsy are eligible for scribe / assistive technology support. Candidates with other benchmark disabilities may also avail scribe support on producing a certificate from a Government health institution (as per Annexure-II). A compensatory time of 20 minutes per hour of examination is provided to all eligible scribe candidates, including those who choose not to avail the scribe facility.

Documents Required for SSC ASO Application 2026

Candidates must upload the following documents with the online application and also include self-attested photocopies with the printed hard copy forwarded by the department. Original documents should not be submitted.

Common Mistakes to Avoid – SSC ASO Apply Online 2026

Based on typical departmental exam application processes, candidates should be especially careful about the following errors that frequently lead to rejection or disqualification.

  • Using Old SSC OTR: OTR created on the old website (ssc.nic.in) will not work on ssc.gov.in. Candidates must create a new OTR on the new website before applying.
  • Not forwarding hard copy through HoD/HoO: Online submission alone is not enough. The printed application must be forwarded by the Head of Department or Head of Office and must reach SSC NR by 23 July 2026. Failure to do this renders the application void.
  • Uploading pre-existing photographs: The portal requires a live photograph captured at the time of application. Uploading a pre-existing photo will lead to summary rejection.
  • Miniature or blurred signatures: Signatures must occupy at least 80% of the signature box and must be clear. Miniature signatures are the most common reason for rejection.
  • Mismatch in personal details: Name, date of birth, father's name, and mother's name in the application must exactly match the Matriculation certificate. Any discrepancy can cancel your candidature.
  • Submitting multiple applications: Only one application is allowed per candidate. Multiple submissions may lead to rejection of all applications.
  • Not verifying service eligibility before applying: Candidates must confirm they have completed six years of approved service in the feeder grade as on 01 July 2025 before applying.
  • Changing appearance before the exam: The appearance on exam day must match the photograph in the application form. Examination staff may deny entry to candidates with noticeably different appearances.
  • Carrying electronic devices: Mobile phones, Bluetooth devices, or any electronic gadget in the examination hall attracts a debarment of 3–5 years.

RRB Technician Eligibility Criteria 2026

Anyone wondering who can apply for RRB Technician 2026 should know that eligibility depends on educational qualification, age limit, and medical standards specific to each post. The qualification requirements vary by department, and candidates must satisfy these conditions on or before the closing date, 29 July 2026, since those awaiting final results are not eligible to apply.

Educational Qualification

For Technician Grade-I Signal, candidates need a Bachelor of Science in Physics/Electronics/Computer Science/Information Technology/Instrumentation, a three-year diploma in Engineering, or a Degree in Engineering in these streams. For most Technician Grade-III posts, candidates need Matriculation/SSLC plus ITI from NCVT/SCVT or Matriculation/SSLC plus Course Completed Act Apprenticeship in the relevant trade (such as Fitter, Welder, Electrician, Machinist, Carpenter, or Blacksmith, depending on the post applied for).

Age Relaxation

Candidates from reserved categories get standard relaxation in the upper age limit: 5 years for SC/ST, 3 years for OBC-NCL, and additional relaxation for PwBD candidates (10 years for UR/EWS, 13 years for OBC-NCL, 15 years for SC/ST). Ex-servicemen get age relaxation equal to their length of service plus 3 years (UR/EWS), 6 years (OBC-NCL), or 8 years (SC/ST) after deducting service length from their actual age.

RRB Technician Application Fee 2026

RRB Technician Selection Process 2026

Candidates often ask how RRB selects Technicians, and the answer is a three-stage process based purely on merit. The recruitment involves a Computer Based Test (CBT), Document Verification (DV), and a Medical Examination, with shortlisting at each stage determined by performance in the previous one.

  1. Computer Based Test (CBT): A single CBT of 90 minutes with 100 questions and negative marking of 1/3rd mark per wrong answer. Minimum qualifying marks are 40% (UR/EWS), 30% (OBC-NCL/SC), and 25% (ST).
  2. Document Verification (DV): Candidates are shortlisted at a 1:1 ratio against vacancies based on CBT merit, RRB-wise. Original documents must be produced; no extra time is given for missing certificates.
  3. Medical Examination (ME): Conducted by Railway Medical Authorities as per the medical standard (A3, B1, B2, or C1) prescribed for the specific post.

Based on typical RRB recruitment cycles, CBT is expected a few months after the application closes, followed by DV and medical examination in subsequent phases - though exact dates will be announced on official RRB websites.

  1. Visit the official RRB website relevant to your region or the centralised portal at rrb.indianrailways.gov.in.
  2. Click on "Create an Account" and enter your name, father's name, mother's name, and date of birth exactly as per your Matriculation certificate.
  3. Use DigiLocker or Aadhaar for identity authentication to ensure smoother verification later.
  4. Log in and fill the online application form, selecting your preferred RRB and Pay Level (5 or 2).
  5. Provide order of preference for posts under the chosen RRB and Pay Level.
  6. Capture your live photograph through webcam or mobile camera as instructed (pre-existing photos are not accepted).
  7. Upload your signature in JPG/JPEG format (30–49 KB, black ink on white paper, running handwriting).
  8. Pay the examination fee online through net banking, debit/credit card, or UPI.
  9. Submit the application and save the registration number for future reference.

Common Mistakes to Avoid While Applying for RRB Technician 2026

Many candidates lose their candidature due to avoidable errors rather than ineligibility. Being aware of these common pitfalls can help applicants submit a clean, error-free application the first time.

  • Entering wrong name/DOB: Details in "Create an Account" cannot be changed later - always match them exactly with your Matriculation certificate.
  • Applying to multiple RRBs for the same Pay Level: This leads to rejection of all applications and debarment from future RRB/RRC exams.
  • Uploading a pre-existing or printed photo: Only live-captured photographs are accepted; printed photo uploads cause summary rejection.
  • Signature in capital/block letters: Signatures must be in cursive running handwriting with black ink - block letters are grounds for rejection.
  • Missing the fee payment deadline: Fee must be paid by 31 July 2026, two days after the application deadline - don't assume submission alone is enough.
  • Ignoring the modification window: Errors (other than account details and chosen RRB) can be corrected only between 1–10 August 2026 by paying ₹250 per modification.

State Bank of India has released the official notification for SBI PO Recruitment 2026, inviting online applications for 1500 Probationary Officer (PO) vacancies under Advertisement No. CRPD/PO/2026-27/09. Online registration is open from 18 June 2026 to 8 July 2026. Graduates in any discipline aged 21 to 30 years (as on 01 April 2026) can apply through SBI's official careers portal, with selection through Prelims, Mains, and an Interview process.

SBI PO Recruitment 2026 Notification PDF Out

SBI's Central Recruitment & Promotion Department, Corporate Centre, Mumbai, has officially issued the SBI PO Recruitment 2026 notification, dated 18 June 2026, under Advertisement No. CRPD/PO/2026-27/09. The notification announces 1500 Probationary Officer vacancies and lays out the complete eligibility criteria, exam pattern, and application process for the post. Candidates can access the PDF Download Link of the detailed advertisement directly from SBI's official careers page before starting their online application, since the notification advises every applicant to read it carefully before applying.

  • Download SBI PO Recruitment 2026 Notification PDF

Why Join SBI as a Probationary Officer?

This section answers why thousands of graduates target the SBI PO exam every year as one of India's most sought-after banking careers. Selected candidates step into leadership-track roles from day one, with the bank highlighting accelerated career progression, nationwide and international postings, structured leadership-development training, and exposure to modern digital banking operations. The role also comes with strong job security, an attractive compensation package, and a clear promotion path that can take meritorious officers up to Top Management Grade over time.

Overview: SBI PO Recruitment 2026

Selection Process Prelims → Mains → Psychometric Test, Group Exercise & Interview
Starting Basic Pay Rs 48,480 (JMGS-I scale)

Apply Online Mode Online only, via SBI careers portal

SBI PO Important Dates 2026

Candidates need to track a single, fairly long registration window for this recruitment, along with the tentative dates for each subsequent exam phase. Online registration and fee payment run from 18 June 2026 to 8 July 2026, and the bank has also released a tentative schedule for the Preliminary Examination, Main Examination, and the final interview stage so candidates can plan their preparation timeline in advance.

SBI PO Vacancy 2026: Category-Wise Breakdown of 1500 Posts

SBI has notified a total of 1500 Probationary Officer vacancies, made up of 1446 regular vacancies and 54 backlog vacancies, spread across the SC, ST, OBC, EWS, and UR categories. The Unreserved (UR) category carries the largest share with 588 vacancies, followed by OBC with 390, SC with 234 (including 18 backlog), ST with 144 (including 36 backlog), and EWS with 144 vacancies. The bank has clarified that these numbers are provisional and may vary based on its actual requirement.

A separate horizontal reservation is available for Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD) within the above categories, in line with Section 34 of the RPwD Act, 2016. SBI PO Eligibility Criteria 2026

Eligibility for the SBI PO post is built on two pillars: an age limit checked as on a fixed cut-off date, and an academic qualification checked as on a separate, later cut-off date. Candidates must satisfy both conditions independently to be considered eligible for this recruitment.

SBI PO Age Limit 2026: 21 to 30 Years

Candidates applying for SBI PO Recruitment 2026 must be not below 21 years and not above 30 years as on 01 April 2026, meaning they must have been born between 02 April 1996 and 01 April 2005 (both dates inclusive). Age relaxation is available to specific categories, but the notification clarifies that cumulative age relaxation across multiple categories is not permitted.

SBI PO Age Limit 2026: Category Wise Relaxation & Eligibility

SBI PO Educational Qualification 2026

Candidates need a Graduation degree in any discipline from a recognised university, or an equivalent qualification recognised by the Central Government, as on 30 September 2026. Final-year or final-semester students can also apply provisionally, but they must produce proof of having passed the graduation examination on or before 30 September 2026 if shortlisted for interview. Candidates holding professional qualifications such as Medical, Engineering, Chartered Accountancy, or Cost Accountancy, as well as those with an Integrated Dual Degree (IDD) passed by the cut-off date, are also eligible.

Number of Attempts Allowed in SBI PO Exam

SBI has fixed a maximum number of attempts permissible for this exam based on category, and candidates who have already exhausted their permissible chances are not eligible to apply again. Appearing in the Main Examination counts as one attempt, while appearing only in the Preliminary Examination does not count as an attempt.

SBI PO Application Fee 2026

The application fee for SBI PO Recruitment 2026 is Rs 750 for Unreserved (UR), EWS, and OBC candidates, while SC, ST, and PwBD candidates are exempted from paying any fee. This fee is non-refundable once paid and cannot be carried forward or held in reserve for any other examination, so candidates should confirm their category and details before making the payment.

SBI PO Previous Year Question Papers: Download PDF Here

CIBIL Score Requirement for SBI PO Candidates

A distinctive eligibility condition for this recruitment relates to credit history, since SBI PO is a banking role with financial responsibility. Candidates who have defaulted on repayment under any loan, NBFC, or financial institution arrangement, including credit card dues, and whose accounts reflect adverse credit history in CIBIL or another recognised credit agency, must regularise or repay all outstanding dues on or before the date of joining the Bank. If the adverse status has not been updated in CIBIL records by the joining date, candidates must either get the status updated or produce a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the lender confirming there are no outstanding dues; failure to do so will render the candidate ineligible and the offer of appointment will be withdrawn. Candidates are advised to check their CIBIL score before applying.

SBI PO Selection Process 2026: Prelims, Mains & Interview

Selection for SBI PO Recruitment 2026 follows a three-phase process: Phase-I Preliminary Examination, Phase-II Main Examination, and Phase-III Psychometric Test, Group Exercise & Interview. Candidates must clear each phase to be considered for the next, and only the marks from Phase-II and Phase-III are carried forward to prepare the final merit list.

Phase-I: SBI PO Prelims Exam Pattern 2026

The Preliminary Examination is an online objective test carrying 100 marks, to be completed in 1 hour, with separate timing for each of its three sections. There is no sectional cut-off in the Preliminary Exam, but a category-wise merit list is prepared based on the aggregate score, and candidates numbering approximately 10 times the vacancies in each category are shortlisted for the Main Exam.

Section No. of Questions Marks Duration
English Language 40 - 20 minutes
Quantitative Aptitude 30 - 20 minutes
Reasoning Ability 30 - 20 minutes
Total 100 100 1 hour

Phase-II: SBI PO Mains Exam Pattern 2026

The Main Examination is conducted online and consists of an Objective Test of 200 marks and a Descriptive Test of 30 marks, taken together in 3 hours 30 minutes. The descriptive paper is administered immediately after the objective test, and candidates must type their answers directly on the computer.

Section No. of Questions Max Marks Duration
Reasoning & Computer Aptitude 40 60 50 minutes
Data Analysis & Interpretation 30 60 45 minutes
General Awareness / Economy / Banking Knowledge 60 60 45 minutes
English Language 40 20 40 minutes
Objective Test Total 170 200 3 hours
Descriptive Test (Email / Situation Analysis / Report or Precis Writing) 3 30 30 minutes
Grand Total 230 3 hours 30 minutes  

Each candidate must score a minimum qualifying mark in every individual section, including the descriptive paper, with sectional cut-offs decided by the Bank based on vacancies. A category-wise merit list is then prepared from the aggregate Main Exam score, and candidates numbering approximately 3 times the category-wise vacancies are shortlisted for Phase-III.

There is also a penalty for wrong answers in both the Preliminary and Main objective tests: for every wrong answer, 1/4th of the marks assigned to that question is deducted, while unattempted questions carry no penalty.

Phase-III: Psychometric Test, Group Exercise & Interview

Shortlisted candidates undergo a Psychometric Test for personality profiling, followed by a Group Exercise (20 marks) and a Personal Interview (30 marks), totalling 50 marks. The Psychometric Test findings are shared with the interview panel to give a fuller perspective on each candidate, and all questions in this test are mandatory.

Final Merit List and Normalisation

The marks from Phase-II (Main Exam, both Objective and Descriptive) and Phase-III (Group Exercise & Interview) are normalised to 100 marks each before being combined into the final merit list; marks from the Preliminary Exam are not added at this stage.

Component Maximum Marks Normalised Marks
Main Examination (Objective + Descriptive) 230 75
Group Exercise & Interview 50 25
Total 280 100

If two or more candidates score identical marks at the cut-off point in the final merit list, they are ranked according to age in descending order, meaning the older candidate is placed higher.
