DSSSB Recruitment 2026 - Application Fee

The application fee is ₹100 (One Hundred only). Women candidates and candidates belonging to SC, ST, PwBD, and Ex-Serviceman categories are fully exempted from paying the fee. Ex-Servicemen who have already secured regular civil employment under the Central Government or Government of NCT of Delhi after availing ESM reservation benefits are not eligible for fee exemption.

Payment must be made only through SBI ePay. No other payment mode will be accepted, and fees paid will not be refunded under any circumstances.

DSSSB Recruitment 2026 - Selection Process

Selection will be made through a Computer Based Written Examination under one of three examination schemes depending on the post applied for.

One Tier General (I-T-G) — Post Codes 34/26, 39/26, 40/26: Duration: 2 hours | 200 MCQs | 200 marks. Five sections of 40 marks each: General Awareness, General Intelligence & Reasoning Ability, Arithmetical & Numerical Ability, Hindi Language & Comprehension, and English Language & Comprehension. Final merit is based on written examination marks only.

One Tier Technical (I-T-T) — Post Codes 21/26 to 31/26, 32/26, 33/26, 35/26 to 38/26, 45/26: Duration: 2 hours | 200 MCQs | 200 marks. Section A: 100 marks covering General Awareness, Reasoning, Arithmetic, Hindi, and English (20 marks each). Section B: 100 marks on the domain subject for the post concerned. Minimum qualifying marks apply only to Section B; combined marks of both sections determine the final merit list.

One Tier Technical/Teaching (I-T-T) — Post Codes 41/26, 42/26, 43/26, 44/26: Duration: 2 hours | 200 MCQs | 200 marks. Section A: 100 marks (same five general subjects, 20 marks each). Section B: 100 marks from subject-specific content including teaching methodology/B.Ed. Minimum qualifying marks apply only to Section B; combined marks of both sections determine final merit.

Negative marking applies: 0.25 marks will be deducted for each wrong MCQ answer. Skill Test, Aptitude Test, Trade Test, or Physical Endurance Test may be conducted additionally as per job requirements. Marks will be normalized (if required) using the Score Normalisation Based on Deviation Method formula published by DSSSB vide Notice No. 10(271)/Sec.Cell/DSSSB/18/989 dated 11.07.2018.

How to Apply

The application process for DSSSB Recruitment 2026 is entirely online. No applications sent by post, by hand, or by email will be accepted.

  1. Visit the official DSSSB registration and application portal at https://dsssbonline.nic.in.
  2. If you are a new user, complete the one-time registration process. Note down your User ID and password — the same credentials are to be used for all future DSSSB examinations; do not register multiple times.
  3. Log in using your registered credentials and select the relevant post code from Advertisement No. 03/2026.
  4. Fill in all fields of the online application form accurately. Once submitted, no change or correction — including change of category — will be permitted under any circumstances.
  5. Upload a recent, clear colour photograph (plain white or off-white background, full face, front view, eyes open) and your signature. Blurred or illegible photographs/signatures will result in rejection.
  6. Pay the application fee of ₹100 through SBI ePay (exempted categories need not pay).
  7. Submit the form and take a printout for your own records. Keep the registration number and application number safely.

The application portal will be live from 16 June 2026 (12:00 Noon) until 15 July 2026 (11:59 PM), after which the link will be disabled.

Common Mistakes to Avoid

Candidates applying for DSSSB 2026 should be careful about a few common pitfalls in the online application process.

Photo and signature uploads are a frequent reason for rejection — ensure the image files are clear, correctly sized, and within the file-size limit specified on the portal. Blurred or illegible uploads will cause outright rejection of candidature. If the payment gateway shows an error after fee deduction, do not immediately retry; wait for a few hours to check whether the payment was credited before attempting again through the portal's payment history section. Use an updated browser (Chrome or Firefox preferred) and avoid mobile browsers for form submission, as they may not render all fields correctly. Save your User ID and password immediately after registration and store your application number carefully — all future communications from DSSSB will reference these. Avoid applying on the last day; DSSSB expressly states it will not be responsible for inability to submit due to heavy server load near the closing date.

IHMCL Recruitment 2026 has been announced by the Indian Highways Management Company Limited (IHMCL), an initiative of NHAI, inviting online applications for 30 posts of Systems Engineer (ITS) on a direct recruitment basis. Selection will be made on the basis of valid GATE Score 2025 in Computer Science and Information Technology (CS), Electronics and Communications Engineering (EC), or Data Science and Artificial Intelligence (DA) discipline. Online registration opened on 4 July 2026, and the last date to apply is 2 August 2026. This article covers the complete notification, vacancy details, eligibility criteria, selection process, and how to apply online.

IHMCL Recruitment 2026: Overview

Indian Highways Management Company Limited (IHMCL) is a company jointly promoted by the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) along with its Concessionaires and Financial Institutions, incorporated under the Companies Act, 1956. IHMCL was established to implement and manage an efficient Electronic Toll Collection (ETC) system across national highways and to deploy Intelligent Transport Systems (ITS) for better highway management and traffic conditions. IHMCL is a non-government company that has adopted the IDA pay pattern.

IHMCL Recruitment 2026: Eligibility Criteria

Educational Qualification

Candidates must hold a Bachelor's Degree in Engineering in Information Technology, Computer Science, Electronics and Communications, Data Science, Artificial Intelligence, or a combination of any of the above engineering branches from a recognized University/Institute.

Candidates who are in the final year of their Engineering Degree programme and are yet to receive their final results may also apply, provided they fulfil all other eligibility criteria. Such candidates must submit proof of having passed the qualifying examination in the form of a Degree Certificate or Provisional Certificate issued by the University/Institute by 31 August 2026, failing which their candidature will be cancelled.

Recruitment Criteria

Recruitment is by direct recruitment through a valid Graduate Aptitude Test in Engineering (GATE) Score in Computer Science and Information Technology (CS), Electronics and Communications Engineering (EC), or Data Science and Artificial Intelligence (DA) discipline.

Age Limit

The age of applicants must not be less than 21 years and not exceeding 30 years as on the last date of receipt of online applications. The crucial date for determining eligibility is the last date prescribed for receipt of online applications.

Age Relaxation

Category Age Relaxation
Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe 5 years
Other Backward Classes 3 years
Candidates with 3 years continuous service in Central Govt. (same or allied cadres) 5 years
Persons domiciled in J&K (1.1.1980 to 31.12.1989) 5 years
Persons with disabilities – SC/ST 15 years
Persons with disabilities – OBC 13 years
Persons with disabilities – General 10 years
Ex-servicemen (ECO/SSCO, Group A & B posts) Period of Military Service plus 3 years

All the above concessions are concurrent - if a candidate is eligible for more than one concession, only the concession with the highest permissible limit will be granted. Age relaxation for ex-servicemen is subject to the conditions that continuous service rendered is not less than six months after attestation, and the resultant age after deduction does not exceed the prescribed age limit by more than three years, as per DoPT OM No. 15012/2/2010-Estt.(D) dated 27 March 2012.

IHMCL Recruitment 2026: Salary / Pay Scale

The post of Systems Engineer (ITS) carries an E-2 Grade pay scale of Rs. 50,000 – Rs. 1,60,000 under the IDA pattern. The indicative monthly salary at the starting Basic Pay of ₹50,000 in E-2 IDA Grade would be approximately ₹1,00,000, which includes Dearness Allowance, Cafeteria Allowance, and House Rent Allowance in X Class Cities. This indicative figure excludes statutory deductions such as EPF contribution and Income Tax.

The official notification does not specify any application fee details for this recruitment.

IHMCL Recruitment 2026: Selection Process

Selection for the post of Systems Engineer (ITS) is based on the following criteria:

  • Merit is determined on the basis of the valid GATE Score of the year 2025.
  • IHMCL reserves the right to invite candidates for interview as per a cut-off for the respective category, to be decided subsequently by IHMCL.
  • If the number of applications received is large, IHMCL will adopt a shortlisting criterion to restrict the number of candidates called for interaction/interview to a reasonable number, by a method decided by the Selection Committee.
  • For the final merit list, if two or more candidates in the same category have equal scores/marks, the candidate older in age will be placed higher in the merit list.

Note: Candidates must enter their GATE Score as mentioned in the official GATE 2025 Scorecard (range: 0 to 1000) while applying.

IHMCL Recruitment 2026: Reservation Guidelines

  • Reservation benefit under community categories is available only if the candidate's caste is included in the list of reserved communities issued by the Central Government.
  • OBC candidates must submit an OBC (Non-Creamy Layer) certificate issued during the year 2026-2027, clearly indicating that the candidate does not belong to the creamy layer.
  • EWS candidates must meet the criteria issued by the Central Government and possess an Income & Asset Certificate based on income for Financial Year 2025-2026, issued after 1 April 2026.
  • Candidates seeking reservation as SC/ST/OBC-NCL/EWS must submit a certificate in the prescribed proforma only, from the designated authority, with the caste/community name and spelling exactly matching the central government's notified lists.
  • No change in the community status already indicated in the online application will be allowed.
  • Candidates who fail to submit valid Caste/Category certificates will not be considered for reservation; if otherwise eligible under Unreserved (UR) criteria, their candidature will be considered against the UR vacancy only.
  • SC/ST/Minority Community/Women/Persons with Benchmark Disabilities are encouraged to apply.

IHMCL Recruitment 2026: How to Apply Online

  1. Visit the official IHMCL website: http://www.ihmcl.co.in (best viewed on Google Chrome or Mozilla Firefox).
  2. Click on the "Careers" tab, then "New Openings".
  3. Click on the relevant recruitment advertisement, then click "Online application".
  4. Follow the on-screen instructions and fill up the application form with the requisite information.
  5. Upload all required documents: photograph, signature, Class X certificate, caste/category certificate (if applicable), Engineering degree passing certificate, and GATE Score Card 2025.
  6. Click "Next" to preview the application.
  7. Use the "Edit" option if any correction is needed, or click the final "Submit" button once satisfied.
  8. Upon submission, a Unique Reference Number along with an "Application Acknowledgement" will be generated automatically and sent to the registered email address.
  9. Keep a copy of the Application Acknowledgement safely for future submission to IHMCL along with supporting documents.

Applications must be submitted online by 2 August 2026 (6:00 PM). Applications received through any mode other than online will not be accepted and will be summarily rejected.

IHMCL Recruitment 2026: Important Instructions

  • The posts carry all-India service liability; only candidates willing to serve anywhere in India should apply.
  • Candidates are advised to fill the online application carefully, as no request for alteration/modification of entries will be entertained after submission.
  • In case of multiple applications by the same candidate, only the last submitted application will be considered; earlier applications will be rejected.
  • Any dispute regarding the recruitment shall be subject to the jurisdiction of Delhi Courts only.
  • The number, category, and recruitment mode of posts may increase, decrease, or change, and IHMCL reserves the right not to fill some or all posts.
  • Candidates must not furnish false, tampered, or fabricated particulars, or suppress material information.
  • All selected candidates must execute a Service Bond of Rs. 3.00 lakh at the time of joining, for serving IHMCL for a minimum period of 3 years. If a candidate resigns before the bond period expires, or their service is terminated due to misconduct within three years, they must deposit Rs. 3.0 lakh to IHMCL. IHMCL does not entertain transfer of service bonds for selected candidates working in other organizations.
  • Canvassing or bringing influence in any form will disqualify the candidature.
  • Any Corrigendum, Addendum, or Cancellation to the advertisement will be published only on the IHMCL website, not in newspapers.
  • The advertisement can be withdrawn at any time at the discretion of the Competent Authority, without assigning any reason.

ICSIL Recruitment 2026 Vacancy Details

This notification is issued solely to create a panel of eligible candidates for present and future manpower requirements of various client departments. The official notification does not specify the number of vacancies against each post. The posts covered under this panel are Data Entry Operator, MTS and Driver.

  • Data Entry Operator (Graduate level)
  • Data Entry Operator (12th Pass level)
  • MTS
  • Driver

Eligibility Criteria

Candidates must meet the educational qualification and age limit prescribed for each post to be considered for empanelment. The requirements for each post are detailed below.

Educational Qualification

The minimum educational qualification varies by post, as listed in the table below.

MTS 10th Pass
Driver 10th Pass (Desirable). Must hold a valid Light Motor Vehicle (LMV) license.

The age limit for the Data Entry Operator (Graduate level) post is 21 to 45 years, while the age limit for the remaining posts is 18 to 45 years, as shown below.

Application Fee

Candidates must pay a one-time registration fee before applying for any post through the ICSIL website.

  • Registration Fee: Rs. 590/- (Non-refundable)

Selection Process

Empanelment under this notification is based on the application ID sequence, followed by document verification and, where required, an interview or interaction conducted by the client department.

  • Candidates found eligible after scrutiny of age, educational qualification, experience and other prescribed conditions will be empanelled.
  • Where the client department makes the final selection, empanelled candidates are sent for consideration in a ratio of 1:3, in increasing order of Application ID. Candidates not selected are placed back in the panel at the end.
  • Where ICSIL itself deploys manpower, empanelled candidates are sent as per increasing Application ID for the number required by the department.
  • Candidates may be called for interview, interaction, or any other selection process prescribed by the client department. Absence at this stage will lead to cancellation of selection.
  • Empanelment, a lower Application ID, or participation in the process does not confer any right to interview, selection, deployment or engagement.

Required Documents

Candidates must carry original documents along with self-attested photocopies for verification.

  • Original documents relating to age, educational qualification, experience and identity proof
  • One set of self-attested photocopies of all relevant documents
  • Two recent passport-size photographs
  • Class X Certificate, PAN Card and Aadhaar Card (particulars in the application must match these documents; documentary evidence is required for any name change)

How to Apply Online for ICSIL Recruitment 2026

Candidates can apply for ICSIL Recruitment 2026 only through the official website within the application window.

  1. Visit the official ICSIL website, www.icsil.in, and go to the Career section.
  2. Refer to the "How to apply for current Jobs" link available under the Current Job section.
  3. Enter complete details of educational qualification, starting from 10th to the highest level, along with experience, in the profile.
  4. Ensure the profile matches the eligibility criteria mentioned in the notification for the post applied for.
  5. Candidates can update their profile as needed.
  6. Submit the application within the window: 06:00 PM on 04/07/2026 to 06:00 PM on 11/07/2026.

  • Selected candidates may be deployed anywhere in Delhi/NCR and may be required to work in shifts or rotational duties. No additional conveyance allowance will be paid.

  • The engagement remains valid for the prescribed contractual period or until a regular incumbent joins the post, whichever is earlier.
  • Canvassing in any form, including seeking recommendations or lobbying, will lead to immediate disqualification and may affect eligibility for future opportunities with ICSIL.
  • If any information or document submitted is found false, fabricated, misleading or incorrect, the candidature or engagement will be cancelled without notice.
  • Incomplete applications are liable to be rejected summarily.
  • Candidates are advised to regularly check the official ICSIL website for updates, corrigenda and further notifications.

Candidates applying for ICAI Branch In-Charge Recruitment 2026 must be a Graduate from a recognized University. Educational qualifications must be from a University, Deemed University, or Institution recognized by AICTE, UGC, or the appropriate statutory authority.

Skill Sets Required

  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills with proficiency in spoken and written English.

  • Strong relationship management and conflict resolution skills.

Only post-qualification, full-time work experience is counted. Part-time or freelancing work is not considered. Age Limit

Candidates must be between 27 and 40 years of age as on 30th June 2026 to be eligible for ICAI Branch In-Charge Recruitment 2026.

Salary / Pay Scale

The compensation offered for the Branch In-Charge post varies by Branch Category, based on the minimum post-qualification experience required. Compensation includes Basic Pay, Dearness Allowance (DA), House Rent Allowance (HRA), Transport Allowance, and National Pension System (NPS), along with Leave Travel Concession, Gratuity, and other benefits as per service conditions.

  • Category-I Branches: Minimum 5 years of experience - Compensation of approximately ₹7.45 lakhs per annum.
  • Category-II Branches: Minimum 5 years of experience - Compensation of approximately ₹6.33 lakhs per annum.
  • Category-III Branches: Minimum 5 years of experience - Compensation of approximately ₹5.59 lakhs per annum.
  • Category-IV Branches: Minimum 3 years of experience - Compensation of approximately ₹4.84 lakhs per annum.
  • Category-V & VI Branches: Minimum 3 years of experience - Compensation of approximately ₹4.10 lakhs per annum.

Application Fee

Candidates are required to pay an application fee of ₹250 (Rupees Two Hundred and Fifty only), non-refundable and inclusive of all applicable taxes, through the online portal. An application will be treated as complete only after successful payment of the fee; incomplete applications are liable to be rejected.

Selection Process

The selection process for ICAI Branch In-Charge Recruitment 2026 consists of a Computer Based Test (CBT) followed by an Interview.

Computer Based Test (CBT)

Parameter Details
Mode of Examination Computer Based Test (CBT)
Medium / Language English
Question Paper Type Multiple Choice Questions (MCQ) + Descriptive
Total Marks 425
Exam Duration 180 minutes
Minimum Qualifying Marks 170

Module Name Number of Questions Total Marks
English Comprehension 25 100

Candidates can select their preferred test centre through the online portal. Centre allotment is made solely based on availability of seats and candidate preference, and no request for change of centre is entertained. ICAI reserves the right to cancel or add test cities depending on administrative feasibility.

Interview

Candidates who qualify the CBT will be called for an Interview. The minimum qualifying marks for the Interview are 30. Marks obtained in the Interview are added to the CBT marks to prepare the final merit list. Before the interview, ICAI will verify submitted document copies against originals; candidates with discrepancies will not be permitted to appear. No TA/DA is paid for attending the interview.

Required Documents

Candidates must upload all required documents in the prescribed format at the time of submitting the online application. Incomplete forms or illegible documents can lead to rejection of candidature at any stage of the recruitment process. Original educational certificates and other documents will be required for verification at the time of the Interview.

How to Apply

  1. Visit the official ICAI website and locate the Branch In-Charge Recruitment 2026 notification (Advertisement No. 01/2026/HRD/BHRS/07).
  2. Click on the online application / "Apply Here" link provided in the notification.
  3. Register with a valid, active email ID and mobile number.
  4. Fill in the online application form with personal, educational, and experience details.
  5. Select your preferred region and give up to three branch location preferences.
  6. Upload all required documents in the prescribed format.
  7. Pay the application fee of ₹250 online.
  8. Submit the form and save a printout for future reference.

Only online applications are accepted. Applications received by post, hand, email, or any other mode will not be considered. The last date to apply online is 19th July 2026.

Important Instructions

  • ICAI reserves the right to increase, decrease, or cancel vacancies, or the entire recruitment process, without assigning any reason.
  • Candidates must fulfil the minimum eligibility criteria of age and post-qualification experience as on 30th June 2026.
  • Applications with false information, suppressed facts, or misrepresentation are liable to be rejected, and candidates may be debarred from future recruitment.
  • Candidates should not send hard copies of their application, CV, or certificates to ICAI.
  • Candidates may apply for branches of one region only, giving up to three preferred branch locations, irrespective of Branch Category. Multiple or duplicate applications may lead to disqualification.
  • Selected candidates may be posted at any branch at ICAI's discretion, irrespective of preferences given.
  • Candidates employed in Central/State Government, Public Sector Enterprises, or Autonomous Bodies must produce a No Objection Certificate at the time of Interview.
  • Educational qualifications of shortlisted candidates will be verified from the respective University, Board, Institute, or Organisation.
  • Selected candidates will be on probation for one year, which may be extended for non-satisfactory performance.
  • Canvassing in any form will lead to disqualification.
  • Any notification or corrigendum will be published only on the official ICAI website; it is the applicant's responsibility to keep checking for updates.

Pay, Allowances and Pension

Selected candidates under this Sports Quota Recruitment 2026 receive the same pay, allowances, and post-retirement benefits as Regular Serving Personnel of the Indian Army.

  • Pay and allowances as per the Army Pay Rules, 2017 and subsequent amendments.
  • Pension governed by the Pension Regulations for the Army-2008, as amended from time to time.
  • Other benefits including CSD facilities and medical facilities as applicable to Regular Serving Personnel.
  • Insurance cover with premium deduction as per existing norms.
  • Ex-Servicemen (ESM) status on release from service, along with ECHS and CSD facilities post-retirement.
  • Promotion prospects exist on merit up to the rank of Subedar Major, with further opportunities for commissioned officer rank subject to qualifying examinations.

The notification does not specify exact pay-scale or salary figures; candidates may refer to the Army Pay Rules, 2017 for detailed pay matrix applicable to Havildar and Naib Subedar ranks.

Selection Process

The selection process for Indian Army Sports Quota Recruitment 2026 involves shortlisting based on sports achievements, followed by trials and medical examination.

  1. Applications are received only through Registered or normal post.
  2. Shortlisting is done based on higher sports achievements of the candidate.
  3. Call-up letters are sent to shortlisted candidates via email, indicating date, time and place of selection trials.
  4. Candidates undergo Physical Fitness Test, Physical Standards Test, and Skill Test at the designated Army Centre.
  5. Candidates qualifying the above tests undergo medical examination at the trial site itself.
  6. Candidates declared Medically Temporary Unfit may avail specialist review at a Military Hospital within 21 days; no further appeal is permissible.
  7. Candidates declared Medically Permanent Unfit may appeal for specialist opinion within 21 days on payment of Rs. 10 by Military Receivable Order (MRO); no further appeal is permissible.
  8. The final selection list is prepared from candidates who qualify in all respects, depending on available vacancies in each sports discipline.
  9. Selected candidates must submit a Police Verification form along with the Offer of Enrolment.

Selection is provisional until candidates report to the allotted Regimental/Corps Training Centre and complete their enrolment form.

  • Education certificates with marksheets of all qualifications from Matric onward, ink-signed by the head of the institution
  • School leaving certificate countersigned by EO/DEO (for open school matric candidates)
  • Domicile Certificate with photograph, issued by Tehsildar/District Magistrate
  • Caste Certificate with photograph, issued by Tehsildar/District Magistrate

  • Character Certificate with photograph issued by Village Sarpanch/Municipal Corporation within the last six months
  • Unmarried Certificate with photograph issued by Village Sarpanch/Municipal Corporation within the last six months
  • Discharge Certificate (original plus four self-attested photocopies) for candidates discharged from Indian Air Force/Indian Navy/other Government organisations, with no adverse entries
  • NOC in original plus four attested photocopies for candidates presently serving in a Government organisation
  • Own sports kit and equipment for the skill test
  • Aadhaar Card for biometric authentication at the trial site

Candidates will not be permitted to appear in trials without original educational marksheets and passing certificates, except where the school/college principal provides an original ink-signed certificate confirming the documents are deposited with the institution.

Common Mistakes to Avoid

Applicants should take care while filling and submitting the application to avoid rejection during scrutiny or at the trial site.

  • Sending the application through speed post or by hand instead of registered post — both are rejected as per the notification.
  • Submitting more than one application for the same intake, which leads to automatic disqualification.
  • Mismatching name, father's name, mother's name, or date of birth between the application and the Matriculation certificate.
  • Sharing personal email ID or mobile number with others, since all communication including call letters and results are sent only to the registered contact details.
  • Reporting after 0600 hours on the trial date without valid justification, which forfeits participation.
  • Bringing photocopied, computerized, or photoshopped photographs instead of original developed passport-size photographs.
  • Carrying a mobile phone into the Selection Trials site, where it is strictly not permitted.

How to Apply for Indian Army Sports Quota Recruitment 2026

Eligible unmarried male and female sportspersons must download, fill and post the application form as per the process below.

  1. Download the application form from the official website www.joinindianarmy.nic.in.
  2. Take a print of the application form on A4 size paper only, as per the prescribed format; non-standard forms will be rejected.
  3. Fill in all details in block capitals, exactly as per the Matriculation certificate, including name, father's name, address, sports discipline, and level of participation.
  4. Affix a recent colour photograph and provide left thumb impression and signature as indicated on the form.
  5. Attach self-attested copies of Matriculation Certificate, Aadhar Card, and Sports Certificate(s).
  6. Send the completed application, along with all required documents, through Registered Post only to the Army Sports Control Board address given below.
  7. Ensure the application reaches the office before 1700 hours on 10 July 2026, as late applications will not be entertained.
Particulars Details
Postal Address Directorate of PT & Sports, General Staff Branch, IHQ of MoD (Army), Room No 747 'A' Wing, Sena Bhawan, PO New Delhi-110011
Mode of Sending Application Registered Post only (Speed Post not accepted)

  • Selection in the Indian Army is fair and transparent, based purely on merit; no bribe is required at any stage.
  • Candidates must carry their Aadhaar Card for biometric authentication at the trial site.
  • Entry into the Selection Trials site is permitted only on production of the Admit Card sent via [email protected]; fake admit cards will be handed over to Civil Police.
  • Consumption or possession of Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances is a rejection criterion; zero tolerance is followed for alcoholism and substance abuse.
  • Permanent body tattoos are permitted only on the inner forearm and back of the hand; offensive, obscene, or racist tattoos are prohibited.
  • Sikh candidates whose religion prohibits cutting hair or shaving may retain hair, beard, and moustache as per laid-down specifications.
  • No compensation is payable for death, injury, or loss during the trials; participation is voluntary, and an Indemnity Bond must be signed.
  • Candidates may need to attend the Selection Trials site two to three times and must arrange their own stay.
  • Use of contact lenses is not allowed during the trials.
  • Certificates with overwriting, tampering of seals, or erasure/alteration will not be accepted.

Knowing the full selection process helps candidates prepare for each stage that follows the written exam. Central Bank of India follows a multi-stage selection procedure for apprentice engagement.

How to Check Your RBI Grade B DEPR Phase-I Result

This section explains the exact process for confirming your roll number in the official result document, so you know where to look and what to avoid.

The result has been published as a roll-number list within an official PDF on the RBI website. Rather than depending on third-party lists, always verify your own status directly.

  • Visit the official RBI website: www.rbi.org.in, or the Opportunities@RBI recruitment portal.
  • Open the official Phase-I DEPR Result PDF for the roll number list.
  • Use Ctrl+F (or Cmd+F) on the PDF and search for your own roll number.
  • Save or download the PDF for your future reference.

RBI has also noted a standard disclaimer with this result: despite careful preparation, the Board reserves the right to correct any inadvertent errors. If you spot a discrepancy in your details, wait for an official corrigendum rather than relying on unverified sources.

RBI Grade B DEPR Eligibility Criteria

This section outlines the qualification requirement specific to the DEPR cadre, useful for candidates confirming they meet the criteria before Phase-II.

Candidates applying for the DEPR cadre must possess a Master's Degree in Economics, or a Master's Degree in Finance/PGDM/MBA from a recognized university or institution.

RBI Grade B DEPR Phase-II Exam 2026: Key Details

This section explains what to expect in the Phase-II stage, including the exam date, shift structure, and admit card rules points candidates often get confused about.

Phase-II for the DEPR cadre is scheduled for July 26, 2026, and will be conducted in two shifts on the same day. A few important points to note:

  • One exam, two shifts: Candidates must appear for all papers across both shifts attending only one shift is not allowed.
  • Single admit card: RBI will issue only one admit card covering both shifts, unlike exams that issue separate call letters per shift.
  • No logistical flexibility: No request for change of exam date, shift, centre, or venue will be entertained under any circumstance. Plan your travel and stay in advance once your centre is confirmed.

How to Download the RBI Grade B Phase-II Admit Card

This section provides the step-by-step process to download your Phase-II admit card once RBI activates the link.

  1. Visit the official RBI website: www.rbi.org.in.
  2. Locate the Phase-II admit card link under the careers/recruitment section.
  3. Log in using your registration number and password/date of birth.
  4. Download the admit card and verify your exam date, shift timing, and venue carefully.
  5. Along with the admit card, RBI will also release an Information Handout for Phase-II, plus separate instructions for PwBD candidates using a scribe or compensatory time, and for candidates with specified disability (less than 40%) who have difficulty writing.

RBI Grade B Selection Process

This section explains the overall stages of selection for the Officer Grade B recruitment, as outlined in the official notification.

According to the official recruitment details, the selection process comprises:

  • Online Examination (CBT) Phase-I and Phase-II
  • Language Proficiency Test (LPT)
  • Final Merit List

RBI Site Engineer Selection Process 2026

Candidates wondering about the RBI Site Engineer selection process can note that there is no written exam for this recruitment. Selection happens through preliminary screening by a Screening Committee, followed by document verification and a personal interview.

Step-by-Step Selection Methodology

  • Screening & Shortlisting: The Screening Committee may enhance minimum qualification or experience criteria to limit the number of candidates called, in proportion to the number of vacancies. Merely meeting minimum eligibility does not guarantee an interview call.
  • Interview Call Letter: Shortlisted candidates receive their call letter only via email from [email protected] — no postal call letters are issued.
  • Document Verification: Candidates must produce up-to-date Experience Certificates clearly stating nature of duties, dates, duration, level/position, and responsibilities, along with category, age, and qualification proofs.
  • Interview: Candidates discuss their anticipated compensation (within the advertised range) along with previous employer compensation details before the interview, which is considered by the Selection Committee.
  • Final Selection: The RBI Services Board's decision on eligibility, shortlisting, and interview results is final and binding, with no further correspondence entertained.

How to Apply for RBI Site Engineer Recruitment 2026 (Apply Online)

Candidates can apply for RBI Site Engineer Recruitment 2026 only through the official website www.rbi.org.in between 29 June 2026 and 20 July 2026. The process requires registration, document upload, a live photograph capture, and online fee payment before final submission.

  1. Visit www.rbi.org.in, go to Opportunities@RBI > Current Vacancies > Vacancies, and select "Lateral Recruitment of Site Engineers on Full-Time Contract Basis in RBI."
  2. Click "Online Application Form" and select "Click here for New Registration"; enter your name, contact details, and email ID to generate a Provisional Registration Number and Password.
  3. Log in and fill in personal, educational, and experience details, using "Save and Next" to verify entries before final submission.
  4. Upload your scanned photograph (20-50KB, JPG), signature (10-20KB, JPG), left thumb impression, and handwritten declaration as per the prescribed specifications.
  5. Capture and upload a live photograph using a webcam or mobile phone QR scan during registration.
  6. Upload supporting PDF documents (20KB-500KB each) for age, category, educational qualification, and work experience proof.
  7. Click "Complete Registration" only after verifying all details, since no changes are allowed afterward.
  8. Proceed to the "Payment" tab and pay the applicable fee via debit card, credit card, net banking, IMPS, or mobile wallet, then click "Submit."

Candidates should submit only one application per post; in case of multiple submissions, only the last completed application with the higher Registration ID (RID) will be considered, and fees paid against one RID cannot be adjusted to another.

Common Mistakes to Avoid While Applying for RBI Site Engineer 2026

Many candidates risk rejection due to avoidable errors during the RBI Site Engineer online application process. Reviewing these common mistakes beforehand can help ensure your application is processed without issues.

  • Writing the declaration in capital letters or another language: The handwritten declaration must be in English, in the candidate's own handwriting, and not in capital letters — non-compliant declarations make the application invalid.
  • Expecting age relaxation: Unlike many government recruitments, RBI has explicitly stated no age relaxation is available for any category in this notification, so candidates must meet the 40-65 year window strictly.
  • Submitting multiple incomplete applications: If multiple applications are filed for the same post, only the last completed one with the higher Registration ID is considered, and the fee from the earlier RID is not adjusted.
  • Uploading documents in the wrong format: Photograph and signature must be JPG/JPEG, while all other supporting documents must be in PDF format within the specified size limits.
  • Not informing current employer: Government/PSU employees must submit an undertaking confirming they have informed their employer in writing about applying, or their candidature may be rejected.
  • Ignoring OBC NCL certificate dating: OBC candidates need a Non-Creamy Layer certificate issued on or after 01 April 2026 — older certificates based on different financial years won't be accepted.

Roles and Responsibilities of Cooperative Intern

Candidates applying for the MSC Bank Cooperative Intern Programme 2026 will be assigned substantive responsibilities at the grassroots level. The intern is not merely an observer - they are expected to coordinate with Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) and other primary cooperatives, and prepare weekly progress reports for the Ministry of Cooperation. This is a full-time programme, and interns must observe the working hours of the concerned bank.

Key duties include:

  • Coordinating with Primary Agricultural Credit Society (PACS) and other primary cooperatives to provide guidance for implementing Ministry of Cooperation initiatives
  • Solving day-to-day problems faced by PACS in computerisation, preparation of business plans, projects, financing issues, and various approvals
  • Preparing and sharing weekly status reports on the implementation of Ministry of Cooperation initiatives, in coordination with the State Cooperative Bank and District Central Cooperative Banks

Selection Process - MSC Bank Cooperative Intern Recruitment 2026

The selection process for the MSC Bank Cooperative Intern Recruitment 2026 is straightforward - applications are accepted offline, and only shortlisted candidates will be called for an interview. Final selection is at the discretionary power of the Bank/Selection Committee. There is no written examination mentioned in the notification.

Step 1 - Application Screening: The bank shortlists candidates from the offline applications received based on eligibility criteria.

Step 2 - Interview: Only shortlisted candidates are called for a personal interview. The exact date and venue of the interview are communicated to shortlisted candidates directly.

Step 3 - Final Selection: The Selection Committee's decision on final selection is discretionary and binding.

How to Apply Offline - MSC Bank Cooperative Intern Apply 2026

The MSC Bank Cooperative Intern Apply 2026 process is entirely offline - there is no online application portal for this recruitment. Candidates must download the prescribed application form (Annexure-I) from the bank's website, fill it in their own handwriting, attach all supporting documents, and physically submit it to the bank's Mumbai head office before the deadline. Applications submitted after 5:15 PM on 10 July 2026 will not be accepted.

Step-by-step application process:

  1. Visit the official MSC Bank website at https://msc.bank.in/career and download the Application Form (Annexure-I)
  2. Fill the application form in your own handwriting with all required details including name, address, date of birth, educational qualifications, MBA/PGDM specialisation, computer proficiency, work experience, and references
  3. Affix a recent passport-size photograph in the designated space and sign in the signature box
  4. Attach self-attested photocopies of all relevant qualification certificates, computer proficiency certificate, and experience certificates (if any)
  5. Provide details of two references - bankers, professionals, or government officials who are residents of India, holders of responsible positions, and not related to you
  6. Place the completed application and all documents in a sealed envelope
  7. Write "Application for the post of Cooperative Intern" on the envelope
  8. Submit or send the sealed envelope to:
    The Joint Manager (OSD), HRD&M Department, The Maharashtra State Cooperative Bank Ltd., Sir Vithaldas Thackersey Memorial Building, 9, Maharashtra Chamber of Commerce Lane, Fort, Mumbai – 400001
  9. Ensure delivery on or before 10 July 2026 till 5:15 PM

Documents Required - MSC Bank Cooperative Intern 2026

Candidates must enclose self-attested photocopies of all supporting documents along with the application form (Annexure-I). Submitting incorrect or false information makes the candidate liable for disqualification and, if appointed, for dismissal from service without notice.

Required documents to enclose with the application:

  • Passport-size photograph (affixed on the form)
  • Proof of date of birth
  • Marksheets and certificates from Matriculation through MBA/PGDM (including Bachelor's degree)
  • MBA/PGDM degree or provisional certificate confirming successful completion
  • Computer proficiency certificate (MS-CIT or equivalent)
  • Any additional professional qualification certificates (JAIIB/CAIIB, certifications, etc.)
  • Work experience certificates, if applicable
  • Details of two references (bankers/professionals/government officials, non-relatives)
  • PAN Card copy
  • Aadhaar Card copy

Important Terms and Conditions for MSC Bank Cooperative Interns

Candidates must clearly understand that the MSC Bank Cooperative Internship 2026 is not a job offer and does not create any right or claim for regular employment with MSC Bank or any associated institution. The internship can be discontinued at any time without payment of financial benefit if the intern's performance is unsatisfactory or if the intern is absent without authorisation. Interns are also bound by strict confidentiality obligations regarding bank documents, policies, and business plans.

Key terms to note:

  • This is a full-time internship programme - interns must observe bank working hours
  • The internship may be terminated at any time without assigning reasons
  • Interns must not interact with media (print/electronic/social media) or represent the bank without express permission
  • Interns must maintain confidentiality of all documents, reports, and information received during the internship - violation entails legal consequences
  • No intern can post work-related content on social media without written permission from competent authority
  • The internship confers no right to employment with the bank or associated institutions

Troubleshooting and Common Mistakes to Avoid

Since the MSC Bank Cooperative Intern application process is entirely offline, several common errors can lead to rejection. Being aware of these before submitting your application saves time and avoids disappointment.

  • Applying while still pursuing MBA/PGDM: The notification is clear - candidates currently pursuing the 2-year MBA/PGDM are not eligible. Only those who have already completed the degree should apply.
  • Missing the 5:15 PM deadline on 10 July 2026: This is not a midnight deadline - it is 5:15 PM sharp. Applications received even minutes after 5:15 PM on 10 July will not be accepted. Plan for early submission or courier delivery with tracking.
  • Not filling the form in own handwriting: The application form (Annexure-I) must be handwritten by the candidate. Typed or printed personal details in the form may be grounds for rejection.
  • Not mentioning MBA/PGDM specialisation clearly: The form has a checkbox for specialisation (Marketing Management, Cooperative Management, Agri Business Management, Rural Development Management). Leaving this blank creates ambiguity.
  • Omitting computer proficiency certificate: Computer proficiency is listed as an essential qualification. Candidates who do not enclose proof of MS-CIT or equivalent certification risk rejection.
  • Providing relatives as references: The notification explicitly states that references must not be relations. Providing a family member as a reference is a disqualifying error.
  • Wrong envelope superscription: The envelope must be labelled "Application for the post of Cooperative Intern." Using any other labelling or no labelling may result in the envelope being misrouted.
  • Submitting only the form without supporting documents: Self-attested photocopies of all qualification certificates must accompany the form. An incomplete application without supporting documents will not be processed.

All five posts under this recruitment are currently notified under the Unreserved (UR) category, with no SC, ST, OBC, or EWS roster points indicated. This section breaks down the category-wise position for each post.

Nature of Employment: Fixed Term, Not Permanent

Candidates exploring this opportunity should understand that these are not regular permanent bank jobs. Bank of Baroda has clearly defined the engagement structure for these IT positions.

Selected candidates will be engaged as an Officer on Fixed Term Employment for an initial period of 3 years from the date of joining. This can be renewed or extended for an additional maximum of 2 years, subject to satisfactory performance and at the Bank's discretion. The engagement automatically ends on expiry unless renewed, and in any case, it remains valid only till the candidate reaches a maximum age of 60 years or the end of the fixed term, whichever comes first.

Eligibility Criteria

Eligibility for these IT leadership roles is assessed as on the cut-off date, and the Bank has linked position-specific qualification and experience details separately for each post rather than listing them within the main notification.

The detailed educational qualification and work experience criteria for each of the 5 posts - VP Head-AI, VP Head Platform Engineering, DVP Dy. Head Cloud CoE, DVP Dy. Head IT Infrastructure, and DVP Dy. Head Platform Engineering - are provided through separate position-specific links on the Bank's official notification, since each senior IT role has its own distinct skill and experience requirements.

General Eligibility Conditions

  • Eligibility is reckoned as on the cut-off date of 01-06-2026.
  • Post-qualification experience of less than six months in any organization as on 01-06-2026 will not be counted toward eligibility, unless that experience is part of the candidate's current employment.
  • Candidates must be a Citizen of India, or fall under specific categories such as a subject of Nepal or Bhutan, a Tibetan refugee who settled in India before 1 January 1962, or a person of Indian origin who migrated from select countries with the intention of permanently settling in India.
  • OBC candidates falling under the "creamy layer" are not entitled to OBC reservation or age relaxation and must apply under the General category.

Candidates often want to know the cost of applying before starting their application. For this recruitment, Bank of Baroda has kept the process completely free.

CIBIL Score and Credit History Requirement

Unlike most government job notifications, this Bank of Baroda recruitment includes a specific financial credibility check. This is an important and somewhat unique eligibility condition candidates must be aware of.

Candidates must maintain a satisfactory credit history, and a minimum CIBIL score of 680 or above is required at the time of joining. Candidates who have defaulted on loan repayment or credit card dues, or against whom adverse reports exist from CIBIL or other external credit rating agencies, will be deemed ineligible for appointment. The Bank reserves the right to reject candidature at any stage, including after joining, if the credit profile is found unsatisfactory.

Remuneration and Location of Posting

Salary for these roles is not fixed on a standard pay scale, unlike typical government recruitment. This section explains how pay is determined and where selected candidates will be posted.

Remuneration will be offered based on the candidate's qualifications, experience, overall suitability, last drawn salary, and market benchmark - there is no fixed pay scale mentioned in the notification. The location of posting is Mumbai or Hyderabad, though selected candidates remain liable for transfer anywhere in India as per the Bank's requirement.

Selection Process

Selection for these IT leadership posts goes beyond a standard written exam, with the Bank assessing multiple professional parameters. No fixed exam date or selection timeline has been announced in the notification.

The selection process may include an online test, a psychometric test, or any other test the Bank deems suitable, followed by an Interview or multiple interviews. The Bank may shortlist applications based on criteria such as suitability for the role, depth of prior experience, leadership exposure, domain expertise, professional certifications, and exposure to regulatory or compliance frameworks. The minimum qualifying mark for the Personal Interview (PI) is 60% for UR category and 55% for Reserved category candidates.

How to Apply Online for Bank of Baroda IT Recruitment 2026

Applications for these posts can only be submitted online, with no other mode accepted. Here is the step-by-step process candidates need to follow.

  1. Visit the Bank's official website and go to the Career section → Current Opportunities page.
  2. Register online using the application format enabled for this recruitment.
  3. Fill in the online application form carefully, since no changes are allowed after clicking SUBMIT.
  4. Upload your Bio-data, scanned photograph, signature, and supporting eligibility documents as per the prescribed specifications.
  5. Verify all entered details, including name, category, date of birth, and post applied for, before final submission.
  6. Submit the application well before 10-07-2026 to avoid last-minute website load issues.
  7. Save the acknowledgement number generated on the portal and check your registered email for confirmation - registration is complete only once this acknowledgement is received.

Documents and Upload Specifications

Bank of Baroda requires specific documents to be uploaded at the time of application, each with strict file format and size requirements. Getting these specifications wrong is a common reason applications get stuck.

Documents to Upload (Application Stage)

  • Resume (PDF)
  • DOB Proof: 10th marksheet/certificate (PDF)
  • Educational Certificates: relevant mark-sheets/certificates, scanned in a single PDF file
  • Work experience certificates, if applicable (PDF)
  • Caste/Category Certificate, if applicable (PDF)
  • PWD certificate, if applicable (PDF)

Photograph and Signature Specifications

  • Photograph: recent passport-style colour picture, dimensions 200 x 230 pixels, file size between 20kb–50kb.
  • Signature: signed in black ink on white paper, dimensions 140 x 60 pixels, file size between 10kb–20kb.
  • Document files: must be in PDF format, A4 page size, and not exceeding 500 KB each.

Documents Required at Interview Stage

At the time of interview, candidates must produce originals along with self-attested photocopies of documents including the call letter printout, system-generated application printout, date of birth proof, photo identity proof, mark sheets and degree certificates, and category certificates where applicable. Notably, a Ration Card will not be accepted as valid identity proof for this recruitment.

Common Mistakes to Avoid

Given the strict, no-correction-after-submission policy of this recruitment, small errors can have a big impact. The following points can help candidates avoid losing their candidature.

  • Do not submit the application without double-checking every field - no changes are allowed once you click SUBMIT.
  • Do not upload a photograph or signature outside the specified pixel and file-size limits, as the system will reject non-compliant files.
  • Do not assume your credit history is irrelevant - a CIBIL score below 680 or any adverse credit report can make you ineligible.
  • Do not delay applying until the last day; server load near the 10-07-2026 deadline can prevent successful submission.
  • Do not carry a Ration Card as your only ID proof for the interview - it will not be accepted.
  • Do not forget to check the position-specific eligibility link for your chosen post, since detailed qualifications differ by role.

All application and update activity for this recruitment happens only through the Bank's official website. Candidates should bookmark this page and avoid relying on any third-party links.

What Is the RRB Exam City Intimation Slip?

This section explains what the exam city intimation slip is and why it matters for candidates preparing for the CBT.

The Exam City Intimation Slip is an official document issued by RRB ahead of the admit card. It tells candidates the city (not the exact venue) where they will appear for the Computer Based Test, helping them plan travel and accommodation in advance. It is a standard step in RRB's exam process and is typically released about 10 days before the exam date, followed by the actual admit card a few days later.

How to Download RRB Exam City Intimation Slip 2026

This section provides the step-by-step process to download the exam city slip from the official portal.

  1. Visit the official website of your respective RRB zone or rrb.indianrailways.gov.in.
  2. Look for the notice titled "City Intimation Slip Link for CBT of CEN 08/2025 (Recruitment for various posts of Isolated Categories)" on the homepage under Important Announcements/Latest News.
  3. Click on the relevant link, which will redirect to the candidate login page.
  4. Enter your Registration Number and Date of Birth (used as password) in the required fields.
  5. Enter the captcha code displayed on the screen and click "Login."
  6. Locate and click on the "Download Intimation Slip" or "Admit Card" link on the dashboard.
  7. Your RRB Ministerial and Isolated Categories Exam City Slip 2026 will appear on the screen.
  8. Check all details carefully, download the slip, and take at least 2-3 colour printouts for future reference.

RRB Ministerial and Isolated Categories Selection Process 2026

This section explains the stages candidates must clear to secure a final appointment.

Selection under CEN 08/2025 is based on multiple stages:

  • Document Verification (DV): Shortlisted candidates must produce original documents for verification.
  • Medical Examination: Candidates must meet the prescribed medical standards for their respective post (for example, Chief Law Assistant requires medical standard C-1).

Aadhaar Verification Requirements for the CBT

RRB has made Aadhaar-linked biometric authentication mandatory for entry into the CBT exam hall. Candidates are required to carry their original Aadhaar card, or a printout of their e-verified Aadhaar, to the exam centre. Without valid Aadhaar verification and the admit card, candidates will not be permitted to appear for the examination.

How to Download the E-Call Letter for RRB Guwahati DV

Shortlisted candidates cannot walk into the DV without a valid e-call letter. This section explains when and where the e-call letter becomes available and what to do with it.

  • The e-call letter download link goes live on the official RRB Guwahati website (rrbguwahati.gov.in) 4 days before each candidate's scheduled DV date.
  • Candidates must download, print, and carefully read all instructions mentioned in the e-call letter.
  • SMS and email alerts are sent to the registered mobile number and email ID once the e-call letter is available for download.
  • Eligible SC/ST candidates will be provided free travel authority as per existing rules.

Mandatory Portal Upload: Signature, Photo & Identification Marks

Before appearing for DV, candidates must complete an online formality that many overlook. Here's what needs to be uploaded and where.

  • Detailed upload instructions are available directly on the portal.
  • The portal remains active until the date of Document Verification.
  • Candidates should refer to the detailed instructions in their DV e-call letter for guidance.

Documents Required for RRB Section Controller DV

Carrying the correct documents is critical, as incomplete documentation can lead to rejection at the DV stage. This section lists what candidates must bring.

Candidates called for Document Verification must carry:

  1. All original documents/certificates, as specified in the CEN and the e-call letter.
  2. Two sets of photocopies of all documents, in A4 size.
  3. No Objection Certificate (NOC) applicable only to candidates currently serving in any Central/State Government department (including Railways or PSUs), including those undergoing induction training or probation. Without an NOC on the DV date, candidature will be cancelled.

RRB Guwahati Medical Examination: Date, Fee & Process

Medical fitness is a mandatory part of the selection process for Section Controller posts. This section explains when and where the medical exam takes place and what it costs candidates.

  • The medical examination is conducted on 16 July 2026, the day immediately after Document Verification.
  • It takes place at a nominated Railway Hospital under the jurisdiction of the Northeast Frontier Railway (NFR).
  • Candidates should be prepared to stay for 3 to 4 days to complete the medical process.
  • The prescribed medical fee is only ₹24, with no additional charges payable to the hospital/health unit.
  • In select cases requiring tests like CT scan, ultrasound, or refractive eye surgery screening where such facilities aren't available at the Railway Hospital candidates may need to pay the concerned lab/hospital directly.

Block Date for Absentee Candidates: Last Chance to Attend DV

Missing the scheduled DV date doesn't always mean automatic rejection. This section explains the block date provision and who is eligible for it.

  • The block date is 27 July 2026, 9:30 A.M., at RRB Guwahati.
  • This is the second and final opportunity for candidates who could not report on their originally scheduled DV date.
  • Failure to report on the assigned date is treated as rejection of candidature, unless supported by documentary evidence that the candidate:
    • Had to appear in a University/Government examination, or
    • Was unwell (sickness).
  • No other reason for absence will be considered.
  • No fresh e-call letter is issued for the block date candidates must attend using the same e-call letter downloaded for their regular DV.

Important Instructions for Shortlisted Candidates

Beyond dates and documents, RRB Guwahati has issued several general instructions that shortlisted candidates should keep in mind throughout the process.

  • Read the CEN carefully: Candidates should thoroughly review all instructions in the detailed Centralized Employment Notification (CEN) and its corrigendum, and retain a record of information filled in their application form.

What Is the RRB Group D Cut Off?

Before checking the numbers, it helps to understand what this cut off actually represents and why it differs across regions and categories.

The RRB Group D Cut Off is the minimum score a candidate must secure in the Computer Based Test (CBT) to qualify for the next stage of selection the Physical Efficiency Test (PET). It is not a fixed number; it is decided by each Railway Recruitment Board zone based on the number of vacancies in that zone, the difficulty level of the exam, and how candidates performed overall. Because RRB conducts the exam across multiple shifts and days, scores are normalized before the final cut off is calculated, ensuring fairness across different sets of question papers.

Factors Affecting RRB Group D Cut Off 2026

Cut off marks change every recruitment cycle. This section explains the main reasons why the 2026 cut off differs from previous years and across zones.

  • Number of vacancies: More vacancies in a zone generally lead to a lower cut off, while fewer vacancies push competition and the cut off higher.
  • Number of candidates appearing: Zones with a larger applicant pool tend to see a tougher, higher cut off.
  • Difficulty level of the exam: Easier shifts result in higher scores overall, which raises the cut off; tougher shifts have the opposite effect.
  • Zone-wise competition: Cut off marks vary from zone to zone since each RRB region has its own applicant base and vacancy count.
  • Category-wise reservation: Separate cut offs are released for UR, EWS, OBC, SC, and ST as per the reservation policy.
  • Score normalization: Since the CBT runs across multiple shifts and days, RRB normalizes scores to keep the process fair before deciding the final cut off.
  • Previous year's trends: Historical cut off data gives a reference point, though the final number always depends on the current cycle's specific vacancy and performance data.

How to Check RRB Group D Cut Off 2026

Follow these steps to view and download your zone's official cut off marks.

  1. Visit the official website of your respective RRB zone (for example, rrbcdg.gov.in) or the unified portal rrb.indianrailways.gov.in.
  2. Look for the "RRB Group D CEN 08/2024 Result/Cut Off" notification link.
  3. Click to open the cut off PDF.
  4. Check the category-wise and zone-wise marks listed in the PDF.
  5. Download or save the PDF for future reference.

What's Next After the RRB Group D 2026 Cut Off?

Clearing the cut off is not the final step in selection. This section explains what happens after the CBT result and cut off are declared.

Candidates who score equal to or above the official cut off are shortlisted for the following stages:

  1. Physical Efficiency Test (PET) - A qualifying-only stage; marks scored here are not added to the final merit list.
  2. Document Verification (DV) - Verification of educational, category, and identity documents.
  3. Medical Examination - A fitness test as per the medical standards applicable to the specific post.
  4. Final Merit List - Prepared after successful completion of all the above stages.

RRB Group D Cut Off: 2022 vs 2018 Trends

Comparing past cycles helps candidates gauge how competitive the exam typically is, though each cycle's cut off depends on that year's specific vacancies and applicant numbers.

In the 2022 cycle, the CBT was conducted from 17 August to 11 October 2022, and cut off marks varied significantly by zone for instance, the UR normalised cut off ranged from around 60 to 70 marks depending on the region. In the 2018 cycle, cut off marks (on the older marking pattern) ranged roughly between 62 and 80 for the UR category across zones. Both cycles confirm that cut off marks fluctuate zone-to-zone based on vacancy count and competition level, a pattern that continues in 2026.

Candidates can download the level-wise and subject-wise provisional answer key PDF from the official website, bseh.org.in, match their responses, and estimate their probable score before the final result is declared.

This article covers everything you need to know about the HTET Answer Key 2026 the release date, direct download steps, marking scheme, minimum qualifying marks, and how to raise objections if you find a discrepancy in the provisional key.

Direct Link to Download HTET Answer Key 2026 

HTET Answer Key 2026 - Key Highlights

This section gives a quick snapshot of the most important HTET Answer Key 2026 dates and details, so you know exactly what to expect and when.

Particulars Details
Conducting Body Board of School Education Haryana (BSEH)
Exam Name Haryana Teacher Eligibility Test (HTET) 2026
Exam Dates 4 and 5 July 2026
Answer Key Release Date 6 July 2026
Levels Covered Level 1 (PRT), Level 2 (TGT), Level 3 (PGT)
Answer Key Format PDF (level-wise and subject-wise)
Objection Window Opens from 6 July 2026

Note: The release date is being reported by BSEH as 6 July 2026; candidates should keep checking the official website for the exact time of release and any updates.

HTET Answer Key 2026: Overview

This section explains what the HTET answer key actually is and why it matters for candidates who appeared in the exam.

Lakhs of candidates appeared for the Haryana TET 2026 examination across two days, and the provisional answer key is the first opportunity for them to check how they performed. The HTET Answer Key 2026 will be released separately for all three levels of the exam:

  • Level 1 (PRT) – for Primary Teacher posts
  • Level 2 (TGT) – for Trained Graduate Teacher posts
  • Level 3 (PGT) – for Post Graduate Teacher posts

Once published, candidates can download the subject-wise PDF for their respective level, cross-check their marked responses against the official key, and calculate an estimated score ahead of the official result announcement.

How to Download HTET Answer Key 2026 PDF?

This section provides the exact step-by-step process to download your Haryana TET answer key from the official BSEH portal.

Follow these steps to download the HTET Answer Key 2026:

  1. Visit the official BSEH website bseh.org.in.
  2. Look for the "HTET Answer Key 2026" link on the homepage or the notice board section.
  3. Select your exam level Level 1 (PRT), Level 2 (TGT), or Level 3 (PGT).
  4. For Level 2 and Level 3, choose your specific subject paper.
  5. The answer key PDF will open in a new tab download and save it.
  6. Match your marked responses using your response sheet/OMR sheet (if issued) and calculate your expected score.

HTET Answer Key 2026: Level-Wise PDF Links

This section lists the levels for which the answer key will be released, so candidates know exactly where to look for their relevant subject key.

Level Post Answer Key PDF
Level 1 PRT (Primary Teacher) To be updated
Level 2 TGT (Trained Graduate Teacher) To be updated
Level 3 PGT (Post Graduate Teacher) To be updated

Direct subject-wise links will be added here as soon as BSEH activates them on the official portal.

HTET Exam 2026 Marking Scheme

This section explains exactly how marks are awarded in HTET so candidates can accurately calculate their probable score using the answer key.

The HTET 2026 exam consists of 150 multiple-choice questions (MCQs) carrying a total of 150 marks. Here's how the marking works:

Category Marking
Correct Answer +1 mark
Incorrect Answer No negative marking
Unattempted Question 0 marks

Key points to remember:

  • Each correct answer earns exactly 1 mark so if you attempt 50 questions correctly, your score is 50.
  • There is no negative marking in HTET, meaning wrong answers do not reduce your score.
  • Unattempted questions simply receive zero marks with no penalty.

HTET 2026 Minimum Qualifying Marks

This section outlines the passing marks required for different candidate categories, helping you understand your qualifying status once you calculate your score.

The minimum qualifying marks for HTET vary depending on the candidate's category and state of residence:

Category Minimum Passing Marks (Out of 150) Minimum Passing Percentage
General / OBC 90 60%
SC / PH of Haryana State 82 55%
SC / PH of Other States 90 60%

How to Raise Objections Against the HTET Provisional Answer Key?

This section explains the process candidates must follow if they believe an answer in the provisional key is incorrect.

If a candidate disagrees with any answer listed in the provisional key, they can raise an objection within the window notified by BSEH. Important points regarding the objection process:

  • Objections must generally be submitted online, along with supporting proof or authentic reference material.
  • Objections submitted without valid supporting proof are not considered by the board.
  • A fee of Rs. 1,000 per question is required while raising an objection.
  • Candidates should regularly check bseh.org.in for the exact objection start and end dates, which are usually announced alongside the provisional key.

What Happens After the HTET Answer Key 2026 Objection Window Closes?

This section explains the sequence of events following the objection process, right up to the declaration of the final result.

Once the objection window closes, BSEH reviews all valid objections submitted by candidates. Based on this review:

  1. BSEH releases the final answer key, incorporating any approved corrections.
  2. The HTET Result 2026 is declared using the final key, confirming the qualifying status (qualified/not qualified) of each candidate.

HTET 2026 Exam: Quick Recap of Eligibility and Selection

This section briefly recaps the exam's background details for candidates who need context on eligibility and selection stages alongside the answer key.

Level Basic Eligibility
Level 1 (PRT) 10+2 with required percentage and a 2-year Diploma in Elementary Education/Special Education/B.El.Ed, or a Bachelor's degree with the required diploma
Level 2 (TGT) Bachelor's degree with required percentage and 2-year Diploma in Elementary Education, or Bachelor's degree with B.Ed/Special B.Ed
Level 3 (PGT) Master's degree in the concerned subject with required percentage and B.Ed degree

The HTET selection process typically includes a written examination, followed by document verification and a medical examination for shortlisted/qualifying candidates.

Once the CBT concluded, the High Court uploaded the provisional answer key along with each candidate's recorded responses so aspirants can estimate their probable score before the final result and Skill Test call letters are announced. How to Raise Objections Against Telangana District Court Answer Key 2026

This section explains the complete objection process for candidates who wish to challenge any answer in the provisional key, including the fee structure and refund policy.

Candidates who find a discrepancy in the provisional answer key can formally challenge it before the deadline. The objection process is entirely online and requires supporting evidence for each claim.

  • Visit the official website and click on "Raise Objection" or a similarly worded link.
  • Log in using your registration credentials.
  • Select the specific question number you want to challenge.
  • Write your objection clearly in English, mentioning the exact answer option and reason for the challenge.
  • Upload a supporting document/proof in PDF format (maximum size: 1 MB).
  • Pay the objection fee of Rs. 100 per question through the online payment gateway.
  • Review all entered details carefully, since objections cannot be edited once submitted.
  • If your objection is found valid and accepted, the Rs. 100 fee will be refunded.

Objection Window: 6th July 2026 to 8th July 2026

Understanding the marking scheme helps candidates calculate their expected score accurately using the released answer key.

Since there is no negative marking, candidates can calculate their probable score simply by matching their attempted responses with the correct answer key.

  • Gives candidates a fair chance to correct errors before the final key is locked.

What Happens After the Objection Window Closes?

This section clarifies the next steps in the recruitment timeline once objections are reviewed.

Once the objection period ends on 8th July 2026, the High Court for the State of Telangana will examine all valid objections submitted by candidates. Based on this review, a final answer key will be published, followed by the declaration of results for the CBT stage. Candidates who qualify as per their category-wise cutoff will then be called for the Skill Test, the next stage of the selection process.

Kerala PSC Final Answer Key 2026 - Special Branch Asst, Excise Inspector, SI of Police, Assistant, Junior

The Kerala Public Service Commission (KPSC) has published the Final Answer Key for the combined recruitment exam covering Special Branch Assistant, Excise Inspector, Sub Inspector (SI) of Police, Assistant, and Junior posts. The exam was held on 06-Jun-2026 under Question Paper Code 054-2026, and the final key is available in Kannada, Tamil, and Malayalam mediums on the official KPSC website.

Add FJA on  As Preferred Source
  • Download Here: Kerala PSC Final Answer Key 2026 (Kannada)
  • Download Here: Kerala PSC Final Answer Key 2026 (Tamil)
  • Download Here: Kerala PSC Final Answer Key 2026 (Malayalam)

What Is the Kerala PSC Final Answer Key 2026?

This section explains what the Final Answer Key is and why it matters to candidates who appeared for this exam. The Final Answer Key is the officially validated set of correct answers released by KPSC after reviewing objections raised against the earlier Provisional Answer Key.

Unlike the Provisional Answer Key, the Final Answer Key:

  • Incorporates corrections after expert review of candidate objections
  • Marks certain questions as deleted ('X') if found invalid or ambiguous
  • Forms the basis for calculating final scores and the main/short list

Kerala PSC Final Answer Key 2026 - Overview

This section summarizes the core details of the exam and answer key release so candidates can quickly confirm they're checking the right document.

Detail Information
Post Names Special Branch Asst, Excise Inspector, SI of Police, Assistant, Junior
Question Paper Code 054-2026
Category Codes 017/2025, 187/2025, 188/2025, 221/2025, 269/2025, 382/2025, 383/2025, 446/2025
Date of Test 06-Jun-2026
Answer Key Status Final Answer Key

Publishing Authority Kerala Public Service Commission (KPSC)

Available Languages / Mediums

This section covers the language-specific versions of the answer key, since KPSC releases separate PDFs for each question paper medium used in the exam.

The Final Answer Key has been released separately for three question paper mediums:

Question Paper Code Medium
054-2026 K Kannada
054-2026 T Tamil
054-2026 M Malayalam

Each version corresponds to the exact question booklet language a candidate received during the exam, so candidates should download the key matching their own paper's medium and alpha code (A/B/C/D).

How to Download the Kerala PSC Final Answer Key

This section gives step-by-step instructions for locating and downloading the correct answer key from the official KPSC portal.

  1. Visit the official Kerala PSC website: keralapsc.gov.in
  2. Navigate to the Answer Key (OMR Exams) section.
  3. Locate the entry for Question Paper Code 054-2026 matching your exam medium (K/T/M).
  4. Click Download next to the Final Answer Key listing.
  5. Match your question booklet alpha code (A, B, C, or D) with the corresponding answer column in the PDF.

Understanding the Answer Key Format

This section explains how to read the answer key document itself, since KPSC uses a specific format with multiple alpha codes and deletion markers.

Each Final Answer Key PDF is structured as a question-wise table:

  • Q. No. - the question number (1 to 100)
  • Alpha Codes A, B, C, D - since KPSC shuffles question order across four booklet versions, each column shows the correct option for that specific booklet code
  • 'X' marking - denotes a question that has been deleted from evaluation (i.e., not considered for scoring, usually due to an ambiguous or incorrect question)

Candidates should first check their own OMR sheet/booklet's alpha code, then refer only to the matching column in the key.

Why the Final Answer Key Matters for Candidates

This section explains the practical importance of the Final Answer Key in the overall recruitment process.

  • It is used to calculate the final, verified score for every candidate.
  • It reflects changes made after considering objections filed against the Provisional Answer Key.
  • Scores based on this key typically feed into the short list or rank list for the recruitment.
  • Once the Final Answer Key is published, no further objections are generally entertained.

OSSSC CRE Prelims Marking Scheme 2026

Before calculating a probable score from the answer key, it helps to know exactly how marks are awarded and deducted in the OSSSC CRE Prelims exam.

  • Each incorrect answer attracts a negative marking of 0.25 mark.

Background of the RPSC SSO (Home Dept.) 2024 Exam

RPSC had invited online applications for Senior Scientific Officer posts under the Home Department from 19 December 2024 to 17 January 2025. The written examination was conducted from 12 to 16 May 2025 across multiple divisions of the State Forensic Science Laboratory, Jaipur, including Biology, Documents, Serology, Cyber Forensic, Narcotics, and Physics.

A provisional (model) answer key was released in early June 2025, with an objection window open for candidates to challenge specific answers on payment of a fee per question.
